What does selling a house in Oak Lawn, Illinois involve?

Oak Lawn has several local steps: a village transfer stamp, a point-of-sale sewer inspection for houses, and a stamp refund program for some sellers. Each step has its own form, so starting early protects the closing date.

The village borders Chicago on the southwest side and had 58,362 residents in the 2020 census. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 56,450, a 3.2% drop from the April 2020 base. It spans about 8.6 square miles with a density near 6,800 people per square mile, which means most homes sit on compact lots.

The sections below follow the order of a typical sale: the village stamp, the sewer inspection, Cook County recording, and property tax.

How did Oak Lawn develop?

The area was first called Black Oak Grove, after a road along today's 95th Street, and was settled in 1835. The Wabash Railroad brought a depot in 1880, and by 1882 the post office and station were simply Oak Lawn. The village incorporated in 1909. Growth jumped after World War II, and by 1960 nearly 20,000 people lived here.

On April 21, 1967, a tornado cut through the village, damaging or destroying roughly 900 buildings and killing more than 30 people. Rebuilding drove another round of growth, and the population peaked at about 63,500 in the mid-1970s. Since 2002 the downtown stretch of 95th Street has been redeveloped with condominium buildings, shops, a Metra station expansion and a parking garage.

  • Advocate Christ Medical Center is one of the largest hospitals and Level I trauma centers in the state.
  • Metra's SouthWest Service runs from the Oak Lawn station toward downtown Chicago.
  • Elementary schools include Kolb, Lieb, Harnew, Columbus Manor, Covington, Hannum, Hometown, Kolmar and Sward, with Simmons and Oak Lawn-Hometown as middle schools.
  • Oak Lawn Community High School and Harold L. Richards High School are the two public high schools.

What do Census figures show for Oak Lawn housing?

Over 82% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median household income is $83,911. The table collects the housing numbers a seller is most likely to compare against.

Oak Lawn housing and income, from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for the village.

Health care and social assistance is the largest receipts category in the Census Bureau's 2022 business figures, ahead of retail at $1,421,717,000. Mean travel time to work is 30.8 minutes.

How does the Oak Lawn transfer stamp work?

The Cook County Clerk's October 2025 list shows an Oak Lawn tax of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, enacted January 1, 1982, with the seller liable and an exemption letter attached to the recording as proof. Exempt transfers pay no fee. The village adds that senior sellers of a primary residence are now exempt, with the rules in section 3 of its exemption list.

  • Request stamps or an exemption letter from the Finance Department. The village accepts only electronic fillable forms, and handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Questions go to 708-499-7775 or transferstamps@oaklawn-il.gov.
  • A Utility Billing Account Change form handles the water account.
  • The village's own address on the Clerk's list is 9446 S. Raymond St., phone 708.636.4400.

State and county taxes sit on top: 50 cents per $500 for the state under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and 25 cents per $500 for Cook County.

What is the sewer inspection and how do I schedule it?

Oak Lawn requires a sewer inspection, called I&I, for single-family homes and qualifying townhomes before the transfer stamp. The village recommends scheduling well ahead of closing.

  1. Use the village's online permit portal, search the property address, choose Residential and the Transfer Stamp Sewer Inspection (I&I) permit type, and enter N/A for work details.
  2. The village reviews the request and emails either a record number with a scheduling link or a note that no inspection is needed.
  3. Pick a date for the I&I Sewer inspection. It happens between 10am and 2pm, and someone over 18 must be present with access to the interior.
  4. After the inspection, a payment link arrives by email for $100, and the results follow once payment is made.

Ask the village's Finance Department at 708-499-7775 whether your address needs the inspection, since the village screens each request first.

Can I get some transfer stamp money back?

Yes, in three cases under village ordinance 3-2-7, each requiring the seller to have owned and lived in the house as a principal residence without renting any part of it.

  • Reinvestment: buy or build a single-family home or condominium inside the village within one year of paying the tax, and live there.
  • Senior citizens: a one-time refund for a seller age 65 or older who owned and occupied the home for more than one year, with a rule for co-owners under 60.
  • Family sale: sell to a child, parent, grandparent, brother, sister or grandchild, step relatives included.

Refund requests are due within one year of the sale. Packets for each case are linked from the village's refund page, and the Finance Department's refund line is 708-499-7777.

How does Cook County assessment and recording apply?

Oak Lawn deeds are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St. The Clerk lists the seller as liable for both the state and county stamps. A PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

For assessments, look up your 14-digit PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to see your township. The south and west suburban townships follow a triennial cycle with reassessments in 2023 and 2026. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for installment status on the parcel, and expect the title company to prorate the year's bill at closing.

What do buyers see in Oak Lawn parks and daily life?

The village maintains 22 parks on more than 300 acres. Centennial Park alone covers 38 acres, and the park system includes outdoor pools, an indoor ice arena, two fitness centers, an indoor racquet center and an 18-hole golf course. Oak Lawn's public library began in 1934 with a collection of one hundred books.

Broadband subscriptions reach 91.3% of households in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, and the median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,000 a month. Those are useful points when a buyer weighs a house here against a rental.

Which sale route fits an Oak Lawn house?

An updated house near 95th Street or the Metra station usually does well in a listing. A house with sewer problems, an old rental history or an estate behind it often fits a direct as-is sale better, since the inspection and stamp steps still apply either way.

More questions about Oak Lawn, IL

Does Oak Lawn charge a transfer tax?

Yes. The Cook County Clerk's list shows a village rate of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, paid by the seller, with exempt transfers needing an exemption letter. Contact the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 for the stamp.

What does the Oak Lawn sewer inspection cost?

The village charges $100, paid by a link emailed after the inspection. It applies to single-family homes and qualifying townhomes and runs between 10am and 2pm.

Are seniors exempt from the transfer stamp?

The village states that seniors selling a primary residence are now exempt, with details in section 3 of its exemption list. A separate refund route exists for sellers 65 or older under ordinance 3-2-7.

How long do I have to ask for a stamp refund?

Refunds must be requested within one year of the date of sale. The village lists reinvestment, senior and immediate family cases, each with its own packet.

Where is an Oak Lawn deed recorded?

With the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The sale also needs the PTAX-203 declaration and stamped deed.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Berwyn, IL sale

Sell Your Berwyn House for Cash

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Berwyn at a glance

Selling in Berwyn?
We buy Berwyn houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What makes Berwyn different from other Chicago-area suburbs for sellers?

Berwyn is a dense inner-ring suburb in Cook County, packed into 3.90 square miles with Oak Park to the north, Cicero to the east, Stickney to the south, and Lyons, Riverside, North Riverside and Forest Park to the west. Its nickname is the City of Homes, and the housing reflects it: small bungalows on the north side around Roosevelt and Cermak roads, larger houses toward the south, and many duplexes and three-unit buildings scattered between.

The ground matters to anyone buying here. Before settlement the area was grassy marshland, with Mud Lake reaching nearly to today's southern border, and the south end flooded regularly in heavy rain during its early years. A sand and gravel beach ridge from ancient Lake Chicago runs along Riverside Drive. A buyer's inspector will look at basements and sewer laterals closely, so a seller with old flooding or backup history should gather repair records and any sewer scope reports before listing.

How dense and how costly is Berwyn housing?

Census Bureau estimates put Berwyn at 55,001 residents on July 1, 2025, down 3.9 percent from an April 2020 base of 57,235. Its density was 14,664.4 people per square mile in the 2020 count.

Berwyn housing and household facts, Census Bureau QuickFacts

Households average 2.71 people, 62.8 percent of residents Hispanic or Latino and 25.0 percent foreign-born. Listings and disclosures that reach Spanish-speaking buyers and heirs are worth considering, since 53.5 percent of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home.

What does the City of Berwyn require when a house changes hands?

Berwyn runs its own transfer paperwork through the Collections and Licensing office and the Compliance Department at City Hall, 6700 W. 26th Street. The city's checklist for quit claim transfers shows what the office looks at, and sellers on a regular sale should ask the same departments which items apply to them.

  • Building: a property inspection is required when all parties are coming off title, any fines or liens must be paid, and open permits must be closed out.
  • Police: parking tickets and fines must be paid in full.
  • Water: the water bill balance must be current.
  • Collector: bring the original deed that will be recorded with Cook County, the completed Berwyn Declaration form and a payment of $100.00, payable to the City of Berwyn by cash, check, money order or credit card.
  • Trusts and corporations: add the trust agreement or corporate papers only if the property is coming out of the trust or corporation, and add an Attorney's Certification form when someone is added to or removed from title.

City stamps are processed at the counter or by mail on four weekdays (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) between 9 a.m. and half past four, and on Tuesday until half past seven in the evening. Mailed packets need a return envelope with postage. The Compliance Department number is (708) 788-2660, extensions 6445 or 6449.

How does a Berwyn certificate of compliance and occupancy work?

Berwyn issues certificates of compliance and occupancy after a city inspection, and the fee depends on the type of property. For residential buildings the city's fee sheet lists $100.00 for a single-family house, $125.00 for two to three units, $175.00 for four to six units, and $70.00 for each unit over six.

Inspections are scheduled in person at the first-floor Compliance Department window in City Hall, with payment due when you schedule and no exceptions. Cash, check, money order and credit cards are accepted. An inspection report stays valid for six months from the inspection date, so time it close to your target closing rather than months ahead. The service window opens at 9 a.m. every weekday, closes at 5 p.m. on four of them, and stays open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays.

Ask the Compliance Department whether your particular sale needs a certificate, because the answer can depend on the building type and who is on title. Buyers who plan to rehab a property often accept the inspection list as part of an as-is price.

What building permit rules should Berwyn sellers know?

The Building Permits Department says permits go out only until half past four on most weekdays and half past seven on Tuesdays. Applications can be submitted in person or emailed to buildingpermits@berwyn-il.gov, and incomplete applications are not sent for director review. Homeowners may do some non-commercial repairs themselves under the city's Work By Owner handout, but the city publishes guides on what needs a permit and on hiring contractors.

Codes the city lists as applicable include the 2024 International Residential Code, the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code, the Illinois State Plumbing Code 2014 and the 2021 Illinois Energy Conservation Code. If a prior owner finished a basement or added a bathroom without a permit, resolving it can take time, so ask for your address's permit file early.

What happens at the Cook County Clerk when a Berwyn deed is recorded?

Cook County deeds are recorded by the Clerk's Recording Division at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 120, in person or by mail. A deed needs the property index number (PIN), the full legal description, the property address, a mail-to address, the grantee's name and address, the name and address for future tax bills, and city, state and county transfer tax declarations and stamps or a stated exemption. The Clerk tells filers to check with the municipality for its own requirements, so Berwyn's own declaration and payment are a separate step before recording.

The Clerk's page prints the stamp history for Illinois: since September 15, 1989, stamps are $0.75 per $500.00, split into $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Only title companies may e-record deeds that carry consideration, while fully exempt deeds can be e-recorded by other filers. A document that misses the Clerk's format standards is charged an additional fee equal to the normal recording fee.

How do Cook County assessments and tax bills work for Berwyn homes?

Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year, and a reassessment notice shows the PIN, characteristics, estimated market value and assessed value. The Assessor's page says residential assessed value equals 10 percent of fair market value, then a state equalizer and exemptions are applied. Appeals can be filed with the Assessor or the Cook County Board of Review.

The Cook County Treasurer mails two installments a year. The Treasurer's due-date page shows that tax year 2025 installments were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, tax year 2024 installments were due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025, and tax year 2023 installments were due March 1, 2024 and August 1, 2024. The Assessor notes that the first installment is exactly 55 percent of the prior year's total. Because those dates move from year to year, read the Treasurer's page or your own bill before choosing a closing day. Exemptions listed by the Treasurer include homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, persons with disabilities and home improvement.

More questions about Berwyn, IL

Does Berwyn require a city inspection to sell my house?

Oak Park at a glance

Selling in Oak Park?
We buy Oak Park houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What are the ways to sell a house in Oak Park, Illinois?

Oak Park owners choose between an agent listing, a sale they run themselves, and an offer from a buyer who pays cash and takes the building in its present condition. Which one fits depends mostly on the condition of the building and how soon the money is needed.

Oak Park is a village of 4.70 square miles that sits against the west edge of Chicago, so buyers here compare it with city neighborhoods as much as with other suburbs. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 52,823 residents, a drop from the 54,583 counted in 2020.

  • An agent listing suits a house that shows well, with updated systems and a seller who can stay out of the way during showings.
  • A sale handled by the owner suits someone who already knows the block, can price the house, and is comfortable reading a contract.
  • A cash sale suits a house with deferred work, a tenant in place, or an estate where heirs live elsewhere. Compare any figure with what a repaired and listed house would net after commission and carrying costs.

How does Oak Park's older housing stock affect a sale?

Most Oak Park houses date from before 1950, and some sit inside a historic district, which shapes both repairs and buyer interest. The village's historical society is quoted as saying that almost all of the housing stock went up between 1892 and 1950.

Oak Park separated from Cicero in 1902 after a referendum, and by 1930 the population stood near 64,000, above the 2025 Census estimate. Frank Lloyd Wright settled here in 1889 and built homes and Unity Temple before he left in 1911, so the village holds the largest collection of Wright-designed residences in the world. Hemingway was born here and spent his first six years at 339 N. Oak Park Ave., which is open for tours.

A preservation ordinance has been in force since 1972 and has been revised since. The village counts about 2,400 historic sites, mostly Queen Anne, Prairie School and Craftsman homes, and it recognizes three historic districts: Frank Lloyd Wright, Ridgeland-Oak Park, and Seward Gunderson. Ask the village's historic preservation staff whether your address falls inside a district before you plan exterior work, a window swap or a porch repair ahead of a sale. A buyer's inspector will also look closely at original wood windows, plaster, wiring and older masonry, so a seller should expect those items to come up in negotiation.

Where is Oak Park, and how do buyers get around from here?

Oak Park lies directly west of Chicago, bounded by Austin Boulevard on the east, North Avenue on the north, Roosevelt Road on the south and Harlem Avenue on the west. Its neighbors are Chicago, River Forest, Forest Park, Berwyn and Cicero.

Commuting is a large part of the pitch to buyers. Five CTA stations serve the village on the Green Line and Blue Line, there is a Metra Union Pacific West Line station downtown, and CTA and Pace buses fill in the rest. The Eisenhower Expressway runs along the south end and leads to O'Hare. Census data for 2020-2024 give an average commute of 31.6 minutes.

Oak Park also uses its own street-numbering system. East-west numbers begin at Austin Boulevard, and north-south numbers start at the elevated tracks just south of Lake Street. Border streets such as Austin and North Avenue match the Chicago grid, which is worth remembering when you check an address on a listing or a tax bill.

Which schools serve Oak Park houses?

Oak Park Elementary School District 97 serves the whole village, and Oak Park and River Forest High School, the single school in District 200, serves it. Fenwick High School is a Catholic college preparatory option run by the Dominicans.

District 97 runs eight primary schools, Lincoln, Mann, Longfellow, Beye, Irving, Holmes, Whittier and Hatch, plus Percy Julian Middle School and Gwendolyn Brooks Middle School. Because the school district boundary and the village boundary line up, buyers rarely need to ask which district applies. The high school district also draws on neighboring River Forest, so the tax bill for an Oak Park parcel includes several separate taxing bodies: the township, the high school district, the elementary district, the library district and the park district.

What does the Village of Oak Park require when a house is sold?

The seller must buy real estate transfer stamps from the Finance Department before the transfer can be completed. The village prices the stamps at $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and the fee for an exempt transfer is $30.

The process runs in a set order, and skipping a step delays the closing.

  • Email the paperwork to waterbilling@oak-park.us for review before you go in to buy a stamp, including the completed Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration Form.
  • An exempt stamp for a transfer with no sale needs the original signed and notarized deed plus the statement by grantor and grantee. Photocopies are refused.
  • For a condominium that shares a water meter billed to the association, file the Condominium Association Water and Sewer Charges Affidavit or a paid-assessment letter.
  • Order a final water reading by calling 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you plan to buy the stamps. No stamp is issued until every village utility charge is paid.

The village accepts a cashier's check, certified check, money order, MasterCard, Visa or Discover for utility charges. Personal checks are not taken. Your title company or attorney usually coordinates this, but confirm who is doing it so the stamp is not forgotten on closing day.

How do Cook County property taxes and reassessment affect an Oak Park sale?

Oak Park is in Cook County, which reassesses homes on a three-year cycle, and Oak Park Township is in the group reassessed in 2023 and 2026. The Cook County Assessor lists the Oak Park Township assessor at 105 S. Oak Park Ave., phone (708) 383-8005, for owners who want help reading a notice.

Tax bills come in two installments. For tax year 2025 the first installment was due April 1, 2026 and the second was due October 1, 2026, according to the Cook County Treasurer. Earlier years ran on different dates, for example March 4 and December 15 for tax year 2024, so the calendar can shift when bills are delayed. Ask the Treasurer for the current due date and for a copy of your bill, and ask your closing agent how the current year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

What should an owner know about selling an Oak Park house with tenants?

Roughly half of Oak Park's approximately 26,000 residential addresses are in multifamily buildings, so a sale with renters in place is common here. The village's Community Relations Division publishes landlord and tenant guidance, and the leases already signed will matter to any buyer.

  • Apartments in buildings of four or more units need a written lease.
  • A landlord must hold at least one month's rent as a security deposit, and deposits in buildings with four or more apartments earn interest when held more than six months.
  • After a tenant moves out the deposit is due back within 45 days, or 60 days if a repair estimate is sent within 30 days.
  • For unpaid rent the landlord gives a written five-day notice before filing in court.

The village's guidance also sets minimum heat of 68 degrees from 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 65 degrees overnight. Call the Community Relations Division at 708.358.5405 with questions about local rules.

What do Oak Park's Census numbers say about the housing market?

Census figures show 60.0% owner occupancy, which leaves a large renter share, and a typical owner-reported value of $465,500.

More questions about Oak Park, IL

Who pays the transfer stamp when a house sells in Oak Park?

The seller buys the village stamps. Oak Park charges $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and exempt transfers cost $30. The final water bill must be paid first.

Can I sell an Oak Park house that is inside a historic district?

Yes. A historic district does not stop a sale. It affects exterior changes, so ask the village's historic preservation staff before you plan repairs, and tell your buyer which of the three districts, if any, covers the property.

How soon should I order the final water reading?

Call 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you intend to purchase the transfer stamps. The final bill is prepared at that point, and the stamps are withheld until all utility charges are settled.

Does Oak Park reassess homes every year?

No. Cook County reassesses on a three-year cycle, and Oak Park Township falls in the 2023 and 2026 group. Between those years the assessment can still change through appeals or exemptions, so read each bill.

What if my Oak Park house has a tenant on a lease?

The lease and the security deposit stay important to the sale. Oak Park requires a written lease in buildings of four or more units and sets deposit return at 45 days after move-out, so gather those documents before you accept an offer.

Where is Hoffman Estates, Illinois, and where did the village come from?

Hoffman Estates is a village in the northwest suburbs, mostly in Cook County with a very small part in Kane County. Of its 21.07 square miles, nearly all is dry land, and mail is delivered under ZIP codes 60169, 60010 and 60192.

German settlers had farmed the area west of Roselle Road and north of Golf Road, then called Wildcat Grove. In 1954 Sam and Jack Hoffman, a father and son who ran a construction company, bought 160 acres and began building homes. Residents voted to incorporate, and the village was incorporated on September 23, 1959. Annexations north of the Northwest Tollway in the early 1960s more than doubled its land area.

The village had 22,238 people in 1970 and 52,530 in the 2020 census. The count rose from 8,296 in 1960 to 46,363 in 1990, so many houses are several decades old, and a buyer will ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are.

What do federal housing figures say about Hoffman Estates?

QuickFacts estimates 50,858 residents in mid-2025, which is 3.2 percent below the April 2020 base. The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 18,537 households of about 2.75 people each. Of the homes, 74.2 percent are owned, and those owners report a median value of $351,900. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,734, and the middle household income is $106,806.

Two other numbers stand out: 35.4 percent of residents were born abroad, and 46.4 percent of people 5 and older use a non-English language at home. In the year before the survey, 90.5 percent stayed at one address.

  • Just over a quarter of homes have renters, so investor-owned and tenant-occupied houses come up in sales.
  • With so many languages spoken, translated showing instructions and listing documents can help.
  • The 2020 count listed 19,160 housing units, and 3.5 percent were vacant.

What jobs and businesses drive the local economy?

The Prairie Stone Business Park, a 750-acre planned district bounded by Illinois Route 59, Interstate 90, Illinois Route 72 and Beverly Road, anchors the village's employment. It took shape after Sears relocated its headquarters there in 1993, and it later added the 11,000-seat NOW Arena, a Marriott hotel and the Poplar Creek Crossing retail center. The Village took over the arena in 2011, and it is home to the Windy City Bulls of the NBA G League. The park also holds a Northern Illinois University branch, a health and wellness center and offices for companies such as Serta, Mary Kay and I-CAR.

A 2023 list of top local employers starts with St. Alexius Medical Center at 2,500 workers, then Siemens Medical Systems and Claire's at 400 each, the Village itself at 370, and FANUC America and Vistex at 350 each. Many Japanese companies also base their U.S. headquarters in Hoffman Estates and neighboring Schaumburg.

A transfer or job change can force a quick sale. Commutes average 28.5 minutes, and Woodfield Mall in neighboring Schaumburg, opened in 1971, turned the area into a major business center.

Which school districts serve Hoffman Estates?

Several districts overlap here, so the assigned school follows the street address.

  • North of Interstate 90, Township High School District 211 serves high school students.
  • In that northern area, Community Consolidated School District 15 (K to 8) serves addresses east of Huntington Boulevard.
  • Barrington School District 220 (K to 12) serves addresses west of Huntington Boulevard in the same area.
  • Residents west of Barrington Road primarily attend Elgin Area U46.

Most of the village is in Harper College Community College District 512. Libraries that serve residents include the Schaumburg Township District Library, the Barrington Area Library, the Gail Borden Public Library District and the Palatine Township Library. Pace runs bus routes that connect the village to Elgin, Rosemont and other destinations.

Confirm the district for your exact address before you name any school in a listing.

What does Village Hall require before a Hoffman Estates sale can close?

The Village's transfer tax dates to 1987 and falls on the seller of any real estate sold or transferred inside Village limits. Payment and the stamp come before closing and recording, and the Village prints the cost as $3 per $1,000 of the selling price.

  • Allow 48 hours of notice so staff can process the stamp, and send applications or questions to transferstamps@vohe.org.
  • Bring the state transfer declaration (PTAX-203/EZ Dec) and the deed or other document going to the recorder.
  • Call the Water Department at 847-843-4824 at least five days before buying the stamp to order a final water bill.
  • Call 847-882-9100 or use that same email to confirm no liens or fines remain on the property and the garbage bill is paid.
  • An exempt stamp costs a $10.00 administrative fee, needs the fully executed deed carrying the exempt language and signature, and calls for a final water reading if ownership changes.

Stamps are sold at the Village Hall front counter at 1900 Hassell Road on weekdays during business hours, or by mail with a self-addressed stamped return envelope. Settle with your closing agent who will buy the stamp and on what day. Stamp questions go to 847-882-9100.

Where does a Hoffman Estates deed get filed, and what do Cook County and the state charge?

Most of the village sits in Cook County, so deeds go to the Cook County Clerk's recordings division at 118 N. Clark Street. The Clerk's fee page prices a deed at $107, which bundles the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a document storage fee, the State Rental Housing Support Fee and a non-government filer fee. Mail-in recording with return adds $5 per document.

In the Clerk's transfer fee table, the seller is liable for two more charges: .50 per $500.00 for the State of Illinois and .25 per $500.00 for Cook County. The statute behind the state tax is 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

ChargeAs printed by the sourceWho is liable
Village of Hoffman Estates stamp$3 per $1,000 of selling priceSeller

Which route gets a Hoffman Estates house sold fastest?

Pick based on how much time and repair work you can take on.

  • Market the house openly. Exposure is greatest, though the sale then rides on the buyer's loan, appraisal and inspection.
  • Handle the sale yourself. You decide everything and also do the paperwork, stamp steps included.
  • Take a cash offer. Closing can be set to your date and the house is taken as is, which suits a tenant-occupied property or one with deferred repairs.

Count backward from closing day. The water bill request, the lien check and the 48-hour notice all precede the stamp, and the stamp precedes recording. Placing the water call first avoids the likeliest delay.

More questions about Hoffman Estates, IL

How many people live in Hoffman Estates?

The 2020 census found 52,530. A mid-2025 estimate from the Census Bureau is 50,858.

What does the Village transfer stamp cost?

The Village prints $3 per $1,000 of the selling price, and the seller pays. An exempt stamp has a $10.00 administrative fee.

Which county office files a Hoffman Estates deed?

Cook County for nearly every parcel. A very small part of the village is in Kane County, so check the parcel first.

How much lead time does the stamp need?

The Village asks for 48 hours of notice, and the final water bill request, at 847-843-4824, should come at least five days before you buy the stamp.

Which district will my Hoffman Estates children attend?

That follows the street. In the north, east of Huntington Boulevard is CCSD 15 for grades K to 8 and west of it is Barrington 220, while addresses west of Barrington Road mostly go to Elgin Area U46.

Which sale route suits a Plainfield homeowner best?

A Plainfield owner can put the house on the market through an agent, handle the sale personally, or hand it to a buyer paying cash who accepts it unrepaired. Price, effort and speed pull in different directions, so start from the shape the house is in and the date you must be out.

Plainfield has grown quickly, so a newer subdivision house competes against many near-identical neighbors, while a home near the old downtown draws a different crowd. Rank these goals before you pick:

  • Getting the highest possible price, which usually means repairs, staging and showings.
  • Closing on your own schedule, which often favors a direct sale with no financing contingency.
  • Avoiding repairs on a house with deferred maintenance, storm damage or a failing system.
  • Handling an inherited house, a divorce sale or a move that cannot wait for a long listing period.

Because a cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal, one common cause of failed contracts disappears. Even so, set any offer next to what a listing might realistically bring, and have the terms put in writing before you sign anything.

How do Census figures describe Plainfield homes and owners?

Plainfield skews toward expensive, owner-held housing. Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 show 88.0 percent of homes lived in by their owners, far above the share in Illinois's larger downstate cities such as Rockford or Rock Island.

The village grew from about 4,500 residents in 1990 to nearly 45,000 by 2020, and the estimate for 2025 is higher again. That pace means much of the housing stock is under thirty years old, so buyers will ask about roof age, HVAC replacement dates and any homeowner association rules.

A median across the village hides a wide spread. A downtown cottage and a newer four-bedroom on a cul-de-sac sit in different price brackets, so use these numbers as background and not as an offer on your own address.

How do Plainfield's counties, roads and location affect a sale?

Plainfield sits in northwestern Will County, and the village limits reach west into Kendall County. That split means some addresses are recorded, assessed and taxed through Kendall County offices even though the mailing address says Plainfield. Check the parcel record before you assume which county handles your deed.

Location is a real selling point for commuters. The village lies roughly midway between Naperville to the north and Joliet to the south, with Romeoville to the east and Bolingbrook to the northeast. The roads buyers care about are:

  • Interstate 55 along the eastern edge, with two exits serving the village.
  • U.S. Route 30 through the center of town, running toward Joliet and Montgomery.
  • Illinois Route 59, which runs north toward Naperville and south toward Shorewood.
  • Illinois Route 126, which crosses US 30 in the center and heads west toward Yorkville.

The land is flat, a legacy of an ancient glacial lake bed, and the DuPage River runs through the village center. Ask your title company whether any part of your lot touches a mapped flood area, because that affects insurance and a buyer's lender.

Which school districts serve Plainfield addresses?

Most of the village falls inside Plainfield Community Consolidated School District 202, but not every Plainfield address does. Parts of the village are served by Oswego Community Unit School District 308 and Indian Prairie Community Unit School District 204, and in Kendall County most of the Plainfield land lies in the Oswego district.

Buyers often search by district first, so confirm yours before you write a listing or describe the house to anyone. District 202 serves parts of Joliet, Crest Hill, Bolingbrook and Romeoville as well as the village. Its enrollment peaked in the 2010 to 2011 school year at 29,254 students and has declined since, reaching 24,737 for 2022 to 2023.

If you have children in a district and need to move quickly, say so up front to whoever you sell to. A buyer who knows your timeline can often accommodate a rent-back period, which lets you finish a school year before handing over keys.

What village rules and history should a Plainfield seller know about?

The Village of Plainfield runs its building permit process through an online permitting and licensing portal, and its Building and Code Enforcement department takes complaints by phone, email or an online form. If you have open work, an unfinished deck or a basement finished without a permit, resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

Plainfield also has a Preservation Commission and a historic preservation ordinance. The village includes Greek Revival homes and Upright and Wing cottages, a school built in 1847, and three buildings on the National Register: the Plainfield Halfway House, the Flanders House and a 1928 Standard Oil gas station. If your house is in the older core around Lockport Street, ask the village planning staff whether exterior changes need review.

The 1990 tornado is part of local housing history. The F5 storm crossed Plainfield on August 28, 1990, damaged or destroyed more than 1,100 homes and destroyed the only high school at the time. A boom of new subdivisions followed in the 1990s and 2000s, which is why so many Plainfield houses share a similar age and construction era. Buyers of those homes often ask about roof age, siding and the sump pump.

How is a Plainfield deed recorded and what does the transfer declaration require?

Whichever county contains the parcel handles the recording: Will County for most of the village, Kendall County for the western part. Each county sets its own fees and document standards, so ask that recorder's office for the current schedule.

Illinois law also requires a transfer declaration. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-25, it must be presented with the deed, or within three business days after the transfer, whichever is earlier, and signed by at least one seller and one buyer or their attorneys or agents. The form asks for the property's value, parcel number, legal description, deed date and type, street address, type of improvement, lot size, any homestead exemptions on the latest tax bill, and whether the transfer is between related parties.

A deed will not be accepted for recording without that declaration, unless an exemption applies under section 31-45. The county collects state transfer tax through revenue stamps. Section 31-15 prints the price as 50¢ for each $500 of value, rounding up for any fraction, and it scheduled paper stamps to end by December 31, 2025 in favor of electronic ones. Whoever runs your closing normally prepares both the declaration and the stamps.

What must a Plainfield seller disclose to a buyer?

Illinois sellers of residential property must fill in every item of the state disclosure report and hand it to the buyer ahead of signing a contract, according to 765 ILCS 77/20.

Section 25 of the same act says a seller must disclose material defects the seller actually knows about, and is not required to hire anyone to investigate. A seller is not liable for an error if the seller did not know of it, believed a defect had been fixed, or relied on information from a public agency or a qualified professional. Fill the report out carefully and keep copies, including any repair invoices that support what you wrote.

  • List known roof, foundation, basement water and drainage problems.
  • Note any past repairs and who did them.
  • Say what you know about nearby issues such as construction, traffic or highway noise.

More questions about Plainfield, IL

Must a Plainfield seller fix things before selling?

No. An as-is sale is allowed, whether to a cash buyer or on the open market, but the Illinois disclosure report still has to list defects you know about. A buyer will price the unrepaired items into the offer.

Which county records my Plainfield deed, Will or Kendall?

It depends on where the parcel sits. Most of the village is in Will County and the western edge is in Kendall County. Look at the parcel number on your tax bill or ask your title company, then contact that county's recorder for fees and format rules.

Does Plainfield have a historic district that limits what I can change?

The village has a Preservation Commission and a historic preservation ordinance. Whether your house is covered depends on its location and designation, so ask village planning staff before you list a house in the older downtown area.

What paperwork do I sign at a Plainfield closing besides the deed?

You will sign the Illinois transfer declaration along with the deed, plus a closing statement and the title company's affidavits. The disclosure report should already have gone to the buyer before the contract was signed.

How large is Plainfield?

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 50,043 people, compared with 44,762 counted in 2020. The village spans Will and Kendall counties, southwest of Naperville.

How can you sell a house in Lombard?

Lombard sellers choose between a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, and a cash purchase of the house as-is. The village, in DuPage County, runs permitting and code enforcement through its Community Development Department, and deeds are recorded by the DuPage County Recorder, so those two offices set most of the practical timeline.

The 2020 census counted 44,476 people in Lombard, making it the largest of the four Illinois places in this batch of pages, with a mid-2025 federal estimate of 44,399.

What is Lombard known for?

Lombard began as Babcock's Grove, named for early settlers on the DuPage River, and took its present name from a Chicago developer who mapped the settlement in 1868. The Galena and Chicago Union Railroad arrived in 1848, and the village incorporated in 1869. A farm family settled on 80 acres in 1837, and their house, since restored by the Lombard Historical Society, was added to the National Park Service's Network to Freedom list of Underground Railroad sites in 2011.

The village calls itself the Lilac Village. A colonel's estate left to the village in 1927 became Lilacia Park, with some 200 varieties of lilac, and the Lilac Time festival and parade have run since 1930 into mid-May. A house near the park or the downtown station can use that identity in its listing description.

What do Census numbers show about Lombard housing?

Lombard has the highest median rent and the highest median home value among the four places in this comparison, and the shortest commute. It also has the largest share of residents with a bachelor's degree.

With 70.8 percent owner occupancy, rental housing is a larger part of Lombard than of the other three places. The short commute reflects the Metra Union Pacific West Line station, the I-88 and I-355 corridors and Illinois Routes 38, 53, 56 and 64. Pace buses use Yorktown Center as a hub, and the Illinois Prairie Path and Great Western Trail run through on former rail lines.

What is the local economy doing for home values?

The village's fiscal year 2024 financial report cites a 9.79 percent increase in equalized assessed valuation, with new construction adding $5.06 million. Retail, manufacturing, hospitality and professional services anchor the economy, and redevelopment projects near Yorktown Center include Lilac Station, Yorktown Reserve and the Summit at Yorktown. Retail sales per capita reached $27,321 in 2022 on the Census table.

Assessed value is one input to property tax bills, so ask the DuPage County Treasurer and Supervisor of Assessments for your parcel's current numbers before you set a price.

Which Lombard schools do buyers ask about?

Lombard's public high schools belong to Glenbard Township High School District 87, shared with Glen Ellyn, and Glenbard East High School is in the village. Elementary and middle schools (kindergarten through grade 8) belong to Lombard School District 44 or DuPage School District 45, depending on the street. Private choices include Montini Catholic High School and the College Preparatory School of America.

Line up the elementary district for your address before the first showing, since it shapes which families look at the house.

What permits and code rules apply in Lombard?

The Building Division handles signs, fire, fill and grade, new buildings, additions, backyard chickens, accessory structures and alterations. Permits can be requested online through the village portal, fees are paid when the permit is ready for pickup, and some items such as residential driveways, fences and new roofs carry flat rates. The division's number is (630) 620-5750.

  • Fences and grading: a permit is required for all fences and for all grading.
  • Exterior upkeep: grass and weeds must stay under eight inches during the growing season, and litter must be cleared within seven days.
  • Vehicles: inactive vehicles must be garaged and RVs may not sit in the front yard from November 1 through March 31.
  • Rentals: owners who rent must supply heat at 68 degrees from September 15 through June 1.
  • Address numbers: they must be visible and legible from the street.

A walk-through for these items before listing can head off an inspector's note. Lombard is a non-home-rule municipality with a council-manager government, so check the village code for local rules before you assume a state rule is the only one.

Lombard's code guide also asks owners to keep waste containers covered, keep items on the parkway only within 24 hours of scheduled pickup, and park vehicles on an approved hard surface, not on grass. Commercial-size trucks are barred from residential districts. Tidy these before photographs, since a neighbor's complaint can bring an inspection.

Which landmarks and transit links shape a Lombard address?

Lombard's older core grew up around its railroad. Today the Metra Union Pacific West Line connects the village to Ogilvie Transportation Center and out to Elburn, and former interurban rail lines are now the Illinois Prairie Path and Great Western Trail. Stops on the old Chicago Aurora and Elgin line once sat at Stewart Avenue, Main Street, Brewster Avenue and Westmore and Meyers Road.

Landmarks give streets a recognizable identity. Cartoonist Harold Gray drew Little Orphan Annie in a restored Italianate house from 1881 on Main Street, the Maple Street Chapel (1870) served as the first town hall and library, and the Helen Plum library on the lilac estate was decommissioned in 2023. Big Idea, the company behind VeggieTales, started in Lombard. Mention the walk to the train, the trails and the park in your listing, because commuters and trail users are the buyers who value them most.

How does recording work with the DuPage County Recorder?

The DuPage County Recorder maintains the county's land records back to 1839, and recording is fee-funded. The posted fee for a deed (Document Class 1) is $86, which the schedule says includes $10 for document storage, $21 for GIS, $1 for the real property fee and $18 for the Rental Housing Support Program. The Recorder's office number is 630-407-5400.

The state transfer tax in 35 ILCS 200/31-10 runs fifty cents per $500 block of declared value, and 35 ILCS 200/31-25 requires a declaration signed by at least one seller and one buyer. Collection of the tax runs through the recorder, and the statute provides that paper revenue stamps phase out by December 31, 2025, with electronic stamps or other indicia after that. Ask your closing agent whether the village or county adds any local fee on your parcel.

When does a cash sale suit a Lombard owner?

A cash sale suits owners who need to sell a house with deferred repairs, a tenant situation or an inherited estate without staging and showings. With median rent near $1,948, landlords holding an older Lombard rental sometimes prefer a clean exit over renovating. Ask any buyer for a written closing date and a list of who pays each recording item before you sign.

Which office records my deed in Lombard?

The DuPage County Recorder, whose records start in 1839. The posted deed fee includes storage, GIS, real property and Rental Housing Support Program amounts. Call 630-407-5400 for questions.

Is a fence permit required in Lombard?

Yes. Lombard's code enforcement guide says permits are required for all fences so the homeowner knows the requirements before buying the fence. Fences are among the flat-rate permits.

Can I park an RV in my front yard in winter?

No. RVs are not permitted in the front yard from November 1 through March 31, and vehicles that are not street ready must be garaged.

Which high school serves Lombard?

Glenbard East High School in Lombard belongs to Glenbard Township High School District 87. Elementary students attend Lombard School District 44 or DuPage School District 45 depending on the street.

What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?

The statute at 35 ILCS 200/31-10 sets it, counted in $500 units of the value on the declaration. A mortgage that stays on the property is left out of the base.

What are your options for a quick house sale in Romeoville?

Romeoville sellers choose between a conventional listing, a sale without an agent, and a direct sale to a buyer who pays cash. The cash route shortens the timeline most, though the village's clearance letter and transfer stamp process applies to every sale. Plan for it early, because the clearance letter expires after five business days.

This page covers Romeoville's setting, the housing numbers, and the local steps that sit between a contract and a recorded deed.

  • A listing exposes the house to the largest pool of buyers and the slowest closing.
  • A private sale avoids commission and leaves marketing and negotiation to you.
  • A direct sale to a cash buyer is typically as-is, with a closing date set by the seller.

What is Romeoville like for a house seller?

Romeoville is a village in Will County, about 26 miles southwest of Chicago, on the Gateway Wetlands just west of the Des Plaines River and Historic U.S. Route 66, now IL-53. It sits between Bolingbrook and Joliet near Interstates 55 and 355. The village was incorporated on January 19, 1895, after residents of the river port of Romeo voted to change the name, and it covers about 20 square miles.

The area earned the nickname Stone City because of its limestone quarries, and stone from Romeoville was used to build the Illinois State Capitol in Springfield. Lewis University was founded on the edge of town in 1934. In 1950 the village had roughly 46 homes. The Hampton Park Subdivision began in 1957 on more than 600 acres of wetland along IL-53, and the 1990 opening of the Weber Road interchange on I-55 set off two decades of rapid building. Population rose from 21,153 in 2000 to 39,680 in 2010.

Romeoville's ZIP codes are 60446 and 60491, and its land falls across four townships: DuPage, Lockport, Plainfield and Wheatland.

What do the Census numbers say about homes in Romeoville?

QuickFacts estimates 41,281 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.2% from the April 2020 base. Housing here skews toward ownership: 80.7% of units are owner-occupied, and households average 3.05 people across 13,296 households.

Much of the housing comes from the growth that followed the 1990 interchange, so many Romeoville houses are younger than those in the older inner suburbs, and buyers tend to compare condition and finishes.

Where do Romeoville residents work?

The village website lists Amazon as the largest employer at 1,824 workers, followed by Valley View School District 365U at 1,300, Green Core at 1,200 and the CITGO refinery operation at 803. Aryzta, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Magid Glove and Safety and Lewis University each employ more than 500. Kehe Foods and FedEx Ground are also named as major employers.

Romeoville is home to over 600 businesses and won a Gold Medal from the International Economic Development Council in 2013 for adding 1,560 jobs over 2012 and 2013. Warehouse, refinery and retail employers sit close to I-55, so a house with easy access to that interchange gives a buyer a shorter drive to those jobs.

Which schools serve Romeoville?

Many Romeoville students attend Valley View School District 365U, which includes Romeoville High School, A. Vito Martinez Middle School, John J. Lukancic Middle School and elementary schools named for Beverly Skoff, Irene King, Kenneth L. Hermansen and Robert C. Hill. Some neighborhoods lie in other districts: students may attend Plainfield East High School or Lockport Township High School.

For college, Lewis University has its main campus on the village's edge, and Joliet Junior College and Rasmussen College both run campuses in Romeoville. Since district lines cross the village, confirm the school assignment for a specific address before quoting it to a buyer.

What must happen at the Village of Romeoville before a closing?

Romeoville's Real Estate Transfer Tax is the buyer's responsibility, but the seller has to clear the property first. To get a transfer stamp, the property must be clear of all debts to the village, including the most current water bill. You request a clearance letter, which starts the process and orders a final water reading. Clearance letters are valid for five business days. A final meter reading is not required for an exempt transaction if the water account is in good standing and the name stays the same.

The village prints its tax as $3.50 per $1,000 of the full consideration price for nonexempt transactions, or a $40 processing fee for exempt ones. Payment can be made online by credit card or e-check, or in person. After payment, you get a receipt with space for the stamp, and the physical stamp can be handed over or mailed. A lost stamp must be repurchased at full price.

A refund is available only to residents who sell the home they live in and buy another Romeoville home as a new principal residence, within 12 months of each other. The Finance Department is at 1050 W Romeo Road, phone 815-886-7212.

How does the final water bill work in Romeoville?

The final water bill is part of the clearance. The village mails it to the forwarding address you provide after closing. The seller's account stays in the seller's name until a final on-site meter read is complete, so give the Water Billing office your closing date and mailing address in advance.

Any unpaid balance blocks the stamp, which in turn blocks recording. Paying the account in full the day the reading posts keeps the closing on schedule.

What state and county stamps does a Romeoville deed need?

State law sets the Illinois stamp at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, sold through the county recorder (35 ILCS 200/31-15). A deed will not be accepted for filing unless those stamps have been purchased from the recorder of the county where it is filed (35 ILCS 200/31-20). Romeoville is in Will County, so the recording office there handles the filing. Ask the Will County Clerk's recording office for its current fee schedule and the county stamp amount, because those figures are set by the county.

Your title company normally prepares the state transfer declaration and delivers the deed with the village stamp attached.

How does Will County bill property tax, and what does a seller owe?

Will County mails bills on May 1 for the previous tax year, and the Treasurer's levy calendar for bills paid in 2026 shows a first installment due June 1, 2026 and a second due September 1, 2026, both with postmarks accepted. Late payments accrue interest under state statute: 1.5% per month on the first installment starting June 2, with the rate stepping up in later months.

For a seller, the practical step is to check whether both installments are paid and to settle the proration on the closing statement. The calendar changes yearly, so ask the Will County Treasurer for the schedule that applies to your sale.

More questions about Romeoville, IL

Who pays the transfer tax in Romeoville?

The buyer is responsible for Romeoville's Real Estate Transfer Tax. The village prints $3.50 per $1,000 of full consideration for nonexempt transactions and a $40 fee for exempt ones, but the seller must still clear village debts first.

How long is a Romeoville clearance letter good for?

Five business days. The letter starts the clearance process and orders the final water reading, so request it close to your closing date.

Do I need a final water reading when I sell in Romeoville?

Usually yes. A final reading is not required for an exempt transaction if the account is in good standing and the name on it stays the same. For a normal sale the seller's account stays open until a final on-site read, and the last bill is mailed to your forwarding address.

Can I get a transfer tax refund in Romeoville?

Only if you live in the home, sell it, and buy another Romeoville home as your new principal residence within 12 months. Owner-occupants who sell and buy outside the village do not qualify.

Which county records a Romeoville deed?

Will County. The deed goes to the Will County recording office with the state and county stamps and the village stamp. Your title company usually files it.

What is Belleville's housing stock like for a seller?

Belleville is the St. Clair County seat in the Metro East, and its housing stock reflects almost two centuries of building. The first homes were simple brick cottages that locals called German street houses or row houses, and later decades added Foursquare, Italianate, Queen Anne and Victorian styles. A seller with a pre-war house here is often selling a property that has had many owners, many repairs and several rounds of wiring and plumbing updates.

The city dates to 1814, when its founder donated an acre for the town square plus 25 adjoining acres so the county seat could move over from Cahokia. It became a village in 1819 and a city in 1850. After the 1848 revolutions in the German states, a wave of educated settlers arrived, and by 1870 an estimated 90 percent of residents were German-born or of German descent. That heritage still shapes the older neighborhoods around the square.

Belleville has three locally designated historic districts: Old Belleville (1974), Hexenbuckel (1991) and Oakland (1995). A separate National Register district, listed in 1976, has 73 contributing properties. If your house sits inside one of them, ask the city's building staff what rules apply to exterior work before you sign a repair-heavy contract with a buyer.

How big is Belleville and what do Census numbers say about its homes?

The 2025 Census estimate for Belleville is 40,237 people, a 5.0 percent decline from the 42,358 in the 2020 estimates base. Fewer people competing for the same stock tends to mean longer waits for conventional buyers, so pricing matters more here than in a growing suburb.

Home values near $141,300 and rents near $1,019 put a premium on condition, so the next two sections cover the city rules that can hold up a closing for owner-occupants and landlords alike.

Does Belleville require an inspection or occupancy permit when a house sells?

Belleville requires a Residential Certificate of Occupancy before a residence can be legally occupied, and the city's Health, Housing and Building Department issues it after an inspection of the dwelling. Its process sheet tells sellers to call for a housing inspection as soon as they decide to sell, because a passed inspection can shorten the closing timeline and help the new owner get the occupancy permit.

  • The inspection covers electrical and plumbing systems, exterior and interior structure and other readily visible areas, checked against the city's housing code.
  • Defects found must be corrected before occupancy is allowed, and a failed inspection means no permit until the violations are cleared and a reinspection is done.
  • All sewer bills for the property must be paid and current before an inspection can be scheduled or a permit issued.
  • The permit step for a new occupant lists a $55 fee as printed on the city's sheet, and the sheet lists $65 per dwelling unit for rental inspections.
  • The number of people allowed in a unit depends on bedroom square footage, so check the allowed count before finalizing a sales contract.

The department is at 2300 West Main Street, Building M, Suite M113, and takes calls at 618-233-6817 (option 1 for inspections). Its sheet gives weekday counter hours from 8 in the morning to 5 in the evening. Its fee figures carry a June 2022 revision date, so ask the department for current amounts. Any new occupant still needs the permit after a renovation, which is worth raising when you compare offers.

What rules apply if the Belleville house is a rental?

Belleville has run a Crime Free Housing program since November 1, 2013, and any owner who leases a unit must register it. The city's process sheet prices registration at $30 per dwelling unit, with renewals due by October 31 each year and fees doubling when a renewal is late.

Owners and managers must also complete the Crime Free Housing class, which the city now offers online, then email the department for a certificate. A leased unit needs a passed inspection, a nationwide background check on the tenant, the crime-free lease addendum and a signed lease before the tenant can obtain an occupancy permit. With a tenant in place, gather the registration receipt, the last passed inspection report and the lease so a buyer's lender or inspector can see the paperwork is in order.

A second failed reinspection carries a $50 fee on the city's sheet. Vacant, tired rentals that would need work to pass are a common reason owners look at an as-is sale instead of fixing everything first.

What do Belleville schools, jobs and roads mean for a sale?

Buyers ask about commutes and schools first, so have the facts ready.

  • High schools: Belleville Township High School District 201 runs Belleville East and Belleville West. Althoff Catholic High School is the Diocese of Belleville option, and parts of the city fall in East St. Louis District 189, Mascoutah District 19 and Freeburg District 77.
  • Grade schools: Districts 118, 119 (Belle Valley), 175 (Harmony Emge), 181 (Signal Hill), 115 (Whiteside) and 70 (Freeburg) all serve parts of Belleville, so the district depends on the street.
  • Transit and roads: Three St. Louis MetroLink stations sit in the city (Memorial Hospital, Belleville and College), and Illinois routes 15, 158, 159, 177, 13 and 161 pass through. Interstates 64 and 255 are adjacent.
  • Employers: Memorial Hospital, Illinois American Water, Empire Comfort Systems and Permobil are among the larger names listed for the city.

Southwestern Illinois College's main campus sits just outside the city limits, and the city's bicycle trail runs from Southside Park to the college and toward the base.

How do St. Clair County recording and transfer steps work in Belleville?

Belleville deeds are filed at the St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds, whose office is at the county building on Public Square. The county's fee table, current for deeds received after July 1, 2023, lists $55.00 with the Rental Housing Support Program fee and $36.00 without it, with transfer tax added when applicable. The office takes cash, check or money order payable to Recorder of Deeds. Mail goes to PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222, and overnight carriers use 10 Public Square, 5th Floor.

Buyer and seller also complete the state's PTAX-203 transfer declaration, which goes to the county office. The state says counties may levy a 25-cent-per-$500 transfer tax and home rule municipalities may add another, so ask your closing agent which charges attach to a Belleville address. Illinois Department of Revenue's Tax Rate Database lists the rates.

Sellers who hold title through an estate or a family transfer should confirm the deed type with the title company before the closing date, since an exempt transfer is recorded differently from a sale.

How are Belleville property taxes assessed, appealed and paid?

Property in St. Clair County is reassessed every four years, and any change must be published in a county newspaper and mailed to the owner. If you think your value is out of line with neighbors, the county's first step is an informal review with the County Assessor's office. Most cases end there, but you can also file an appeal for a hearing before the Board of Review. Bring an exterior photo of your house and photos of at least three similar nearby properties, property record cards, or a recent appraisal, contract, settlement statement or deed. Evidence must reach the Board at least five days before the hearing or the assessment stands unchanged.

The Treasurer sends bills to the owner even when a lender escrows the taxes, and the owner stays responsible for penalties and interest. Unpaid taxes can lead the county to sell a lien. A principal dwelling with no more than six units can be redeemed for two and one-half years, and other property for two years. The Treasurer also runs a monthly payment plan for homeowners with the Homeowner Occupied Exemption, and online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience charge. Before closing, get this year's installment dates and a payoff figure from the Treasurer's office.

More questions about Belleville, IL

Can I sell a Belleville house with failed occupancy inspection items?

Yes, a sale is still possible, but the new occupant cannot get a Residential Occupancy Permit until the violations are corrected and the unit passes reinspection. Ask the Health, Housing and Building Department for the written inspection report, then decide whether to repair, credit the buyer or sell to someone who plans the work.

Who records the deed after a Belleville sale?

The St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds files it. The county fee table lists deeds at $55.00 with the Rental Housing Support Program fee or $36.00 without, with transfer tax added when it applies. Your title company or attorney normally handles the filing.

Do Belleville landlords have to register rentals before selling?

Yes while the unit is leased: the city's sheet requires registration of each leased dwelling unit and an annual update by October 31. Keep the registration, inspection report and lease together so the buyer can see the unit was compliant.

What if my Belleville assessment looks too high?

Start with an informal review at the County Assessor's office, then file with the Board of Review if needed. Submit comparables or an appraisal at least five days before your hearing, because late evidence results in the appeal being upheld with no change.

Is the Belleville population shrinking, and does that affect my price?

The 2025 estimate of 40,237 sits 5.0 percent under the 2020 base of 42,358. At a typical value near $141,300, condition and price both matter, so get two or three offers or a local agent's opinion before choosing a route.

What is the quickest way to sell a house in Oswego, Illinois?

A direct cash sale gives the shortest wait before closing, while a listing takes longer and favors a house that shows well. Selling on your own is the third route and suits owners with time and a good title company.

Oswego is a village on the Fox River in Kendall County, with a small part in Will County, and it is the largest municipality in Kendall County. The Census Bureau counted 34,585 people in 2020 and its 2025 estimate is 39,948, an increase of 15.4% from the 2020 base.

  • Hire an agent if the roof, windows and mechanical systems are in good order and you can handle showings and a financing timeline.
  • Handle the sale yourself if you can price the home from recent nearby sales and coordinate the paperwork the village requires.
  • Take a cash buyer if the house needs work, is vacant, or belongs to an estate. Weigh the offer against a listing price after commission, repairs and the months of taxes and utilities you would carry.

How did Oswego grow from a river town into a large suburb?

Oswego grew slowly for more than a century and then expanded quickly after 1990. Settlers arrived in 1833, the village was incorporated in 1852, and in January 1837 residents settled on the name Oswego by a single vote after the place had been called Hudson and Lodi.

Caterpillar and Western Electric built plants nearby in the mid-1950s, which helped the Boulder Hill area develop, and the home-building boom of the mid-1980s pushed the village limits west of the Fox River. The census counts tell the rest: 3,876 people in 1990, 13,326 in 2000, 30,355 in 2010 and 34,585 in 2020. A drag strip on Route 34 ran from 1955 to 1979 and is still a topic of local nostalgia, though the site is closed to the public.

Downtown has older buildings, including the Little White School Museum, built in 1850, plus brick pavers and landscaping from a streetscape project. Hudson Crossing Park opened on the river in October 2004, and the Waubonsee Creek Promenade completes the downtown work.

What does the transfer stamp mean for an Oswego sale?

Oswego voters approved a real estate transfer tax on June 28, 2022, and the buyer pays it at $3 per $1,000 of the sale price. A stamp from the village is required before the deed can be recorded with Kendall or Will County, even when the buyer is exempt from the tax.

The seller still has a part in the process, because open village bills block the stamp. Here is how the village describes it:

  • The buyer or a representative sends a MyDec or PTAX-203 declaration at least three business days before closing, online or at Village Hall.
  • The village then prepares a Statement of Open Accounts, and any open invoice tied to the property must be paid in full before the stamp is released.
  • After review, the buyer brings the deed to Village Hall at 100 Parkers Mill, open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., and the tax is calculated while they wait.
  • Payment is accepted by credit card, cash or certified check.

A person who has owned a primary residence in Oswego for at least a year is exempt from the tax when buying another Oswego home, but still obtains a stamp. The village's own example shows a $300,000 sale carrying a $900 charge at the $3 rate. The village states the money must go to the water and sewer fund, tied to the Lake Michigan water connection through the DuPage Water Commission. Questions go to TransferTax@oswegoil.org or (630) 554-0864.

Which schools serve Oswego homes?

Oswego Community Unit School District 308 serves most of the village, and portions of Oswego fall within Yorkville Community Unit School District 115. District 308 operates 22 schools, including one early learning center, 14 elementary schools, five junior high schools, two high schools and one opportunity school.

Because the district also reaches Boulder Hill, Montgomery, Plainfield, Aurora, Yorkville and Joliet, a house's attendance zone is not always obvious from the village name. Confirm the district for a specific address before listing, and mention the nearest elementary and junior high on the flyer. The Census Bureau puts persons under 18 at 26.3% of Oswego's population.

What permits does Oswego require for home improvements?

Oswego handles residential permits through its Building and Permits department, and a long list of projects needs one. The village's application list includes basement remodels, decks, driveways, fences, fireplaces, garages, hot tubs, HVAC, irrigation systems, patios, pergolas, permanent pools, sheds, solar, sump pumps and downspouts, and window and door replacement.

Roof, siding, radon and water heater permits go through an online portal called Civic Access, and the other applications are emailed to the department. If you did work on the house, gather the permit and final inspection records for the buyer.

Floodplain rules apply along the river and creeks. Any change to a structure in the floodplain may need a permit, and the substantial improvement rule generally limits an addition to less than fifty percent of the structure's value. The village has a floodplain map where you can check an address, and the village asks owners to contact it before designing a project.

How are Kendall County property taxes billed?

Kendall County mails one bill a year that is paid in two installments, and the 2026 due dates were June 9 and September 9. Those dates have passed, and the county says a late payment is charged 1.5% of the installment per month.

The Collector's office is at 504 S. Main Street in Yorkville, open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., with the telephone at 630-553-4124. The county will not take estimated or partial payments, so the exact amount on the bill is required. It also accepts payment online, by phone, by ACH, by mail, at most Kendall County banks, and in person, and a drop box outside the office is available at any hour. Ask the Collector for your schedule and for a copy of the bill, and ask your closing agent how the year's tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

How does the weather affect an Oswego house?

Oswego has a hot-summer humid continental climate with four seasons, and a buyer's inspector will focus on the roof, gutters, sump pump and heating system. NOAA climate normals for 1990-2021 give an average of 39.53 inches of precipitation and 29.1 inches of snow a year.

January's mean daily high is 30.5 degrees and July's is 84.0. Spring and summer can bring severe weather, including tornadoes, according to the same climate summary. Keep receipts for any sump pump, downspout or drainage work for the buyer.

What do Census numbers say about Oswego?

Oswego has a young, family-heavy profile, with 87.9% of homes occupied by their owners and a median household income of $123,792.

Oswego village, Illinois, U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts (housing and income are 2020-2024 estimates)
MeasureOswego
Estimated residents, mid-202539,948
Households12,243
Homes lived in by their owners87.9%
Typical owner-reported home value$344,500
Typical monthly rent$1,860

More questions about Oswego, IL

Who pays the Oswego real estate transfer tax?

The buyer. The tax is $3 per $1,000 of the sale price, and a village stamp is needed before the deed is recorded. The seller's part is clearing any open village invoices on the property.

How early must the transfer declaration reach Oswego?

At least three business days before closing. Send a MyDec or PTAX-203 to the village online or at Village Hall, and the village will then prepare its Statement of Open Accounts.

Is anyone exempt from the Oswego transfer tax?

Yes. Owners of an Oswego primary residence for at least one year are exempt when they buy another home in the village, though they still need a stamp. Other exemptions are listed in Ordinance 22-54.

When are Kendall County property taxes due?

The 2026 installments were due June 9 and September 9. Kendall County issues one bill, payable in two parts, and charges 1.5% per month on late payments.

Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Oswego?

Yes. Roof permits are filed through the village's Civic Access online portal. Keep the permit and final inspection record to hand to the buyer.

Carol Stream at a glance
