Where is Highland Park, Illinois, and what shapes the housing here?

Highland Park is a city in Lake County on the North Shore of the Chicago area, about 25 miles north of downtown Chicago. Its 12.24 square miles of dry land are split between Moraine Township and West Deerfield Township, and mail goes through ZIP codes 60035, 60036 and 60037.

Lake Michigan defines the layout. A bluff about 100 feet high runs along 6 miles of shoreline, and wooded ravines cut up to a mile inland. Elevations range from 580 to 725 feet above sea level. A house beside a ravine or at the bluff edge sells differently from one on a flat street near a Metra stop, and buyers of every kind will ask about the lot as closely as the building.

In the 2020 count the city had 11,557 households spread over 12,405 housing units, and 6.8 percent of those units stood empty. A mid-2025 estimate puts the population at 30,767.

How did Highland Park grow, and why do so many older houses survive?

Two small lakefront settlements, St. John's and Port Clinton, came first. After the Chicago and Milwaukee Railroad built a depot, a plat was laid out in 1856. Highland Park was established as a city on March 11, 1869, and it annexed the village of Ravinia in 1899. St. Johns Avenue and Port Clinton Square still carry the old settlement names.

The housing stock reflects that early start. The Willits House is on the federal historic register, and the register also lists, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, along with homes by John S. Van Bergen, Howard Van Doren Shaw, Robert E. Seyfarth and David Adler. Landscape architect Jens Jensen lived in the city and designed projects that are on the register as well.

Owners of an architect-designed house usually have the original plans, permits and drawings in a drawer somewhere. Gather them before you talk to any buyer, because documented history is the one thing that can set a house apart from its neighbors.

How common is homeownership in Highland Park, by the federal numbers?

The five-year survey figures cover 2020 to 2024. They give Highland Park 11,787 households, 83.8 percent of them owners, and a median home value of $607,300. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,925. Roughly 87.5 percent of residents stayed at the same address through the previous year, and 24.3 percent are 65 or older.

Those numbers describe a city of long-time owners. Downsizing, estate settlement and relocation all produce sales with a firm deadline. Median household income is $168,094, and workers travel 27.5 minutes on average to get to a job.

  • Because most residents stay put, your listing may be the first on the street in years, so pull recent sale records before you pick a price.
  • Older construction makes for a long inspection report, and a buyer may ask to see original plans and permits.
  • Four Metra stations inside city limits make distance to the platform a selling point for downtown workers.

Which schools and commuting routes matter to Highland Park buyers?

Public schools come from two districts. North Shore School District 112 operates an early childhood center, seven elementary schools and two middle schools. Township High School District 113 operates Highland Park High School and also Deerfield High School in nearby Deerfield.

US 41 is the main highway and connects Chicago to Milwaukee. Four Metra stations sit inside the city limits: Braeside, Ravinia Park, Ravinia and Highland Park. All are on the Union Pacific North Line, which starts in Chicago and ends in Kenosha, Wisconsin. Pace buses add local routes, O'Hare is about 20 miles southwest, and the Skokie Valley Trail runs through town.

Ravinia, the open-air pavilion that seats 3,200, has been the summer home of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra since 1936. Three public beaches, Rosewood, Moraine and Park Avenue, round out the lakefront. Buyers of every type, cash buyers included, weigh the stations, schools and beaches when they set a price.

What must happen at City Hall before a Highland Park closing?

Chapter 97, Article X of the city code taxes real property transfers. The declaration form prints the rate as $5.00 per $1,000 or fraction thereof of full actual consideration, and it puts payment on the transferor when the sale contract says nothing different.

  • The declaration needs a signature from a transferor and a transferee.
  • A final water bill must be prepared and paid when the tax stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be scheduled up to five business days before closing.
  • A copy of the deed headed for the Recorder of Deeds goes to the city, while an exempt transfer requires the original.
  • Consideration counts the mortgage amount and any liabilities the buyer assumes.
  • Section 97.1004 lists exempt deeds. Examples include tax deeds, partition deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and foreclosure or in-lieu deeds to a mortgage holder.

The form says personal checks and credit cards are refused. Finance, at 1707 St. Johns Avenue, takes calls at 847.432.0800 and email at Finance@cityhpil.com.

What does the Lake County Clerk charge to record a Highland Park deed?

The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office handles deeds at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. Its fee page sets $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and says state and county transfer taxes are the only added charges at recording.

The state levies its own tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, charged on the value stated in the declaration, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be excluded when the deed says so. The closing agent will give you the county rate and a final total.

Which selling route fits a Highland Park owner in a hurry?

Three routes exist, and each trades price, certainty and effort differently.

  • Work with a listing agent. Exposure is widest, and a bluff, ravine or architect-designed property can justify a longer wait.
  • Go it alone. You control the contract and carry the showings, disclosures and negotiation.
  • Accept a cash offer. The closing date can follow your calendar and the house stays as it is, which helps with an estate home, a tenant-occupied unit or a house that needs work.

The city stamp, the final water bill and the deed filing apply on every route. Ask for the final reading early so closing does not wait on a meter.

When a cash buyer makes an offer, get in writing who pays each transfer charge named above. The sale contract is where the allocation is settled.

How many people live in Highland Park?

The April 2020 census found 30,176 residents, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 30,767.

Who owes the city transfer tax on a Highland Park sale?

The transferor does, as the city's form reads, when the contract has no clause to the contrary.

Does a Highland Park sale need a final water bill?

Yes. The form requires it to be prepared and paid when the stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be booked up to five business days ahead of closing.

Which office files the deed after a Highland Park closing?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. Its published fee for a standard document is $70.

Which school districts serve Highland Park?

North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools, and Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and Deerfield High School.

Where is Huntley, Illinois, and why does it sit in two counties?

Huntley is a village in the northwest Chicago area that straddles McHenry County and Kane County. It lies along Interstate 90, covers about 14.29 square miles of land, and uses ZIP code 60142. Three townships divide it: Grafton, Rutland and Hampshire.

The village's own FAQ gives the township split. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and land south of Kreutzer Road is in Rutland Township, except the northwest end of Sun City, which is in Hampshire Township. The county and township matter to a seller because they decide which office handles your tax bill and your deed.

Huntley was founded in 1851 and incorporated in 1872, and it is named for Thomas Stillwell Huntley. Its census count was 5,730 in 2000, 24,291 in 2010 and 27,740 in 2020, one of the sharpest growth curves in the region.

What do the Census numbers say about Huntley homeowners?

The Census Bureau estimated 29,132 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.0 percent from the April 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it reports an owner-occupied rate of 88.9 percent, a median value of owner-occupied homes of $334,300, and 12,213 households averaging 2.29 people. Median household income is $88,536, and the mean commute is 29.5 minutes.

The age profile is the most unusual part. QuickFacts lists 34.1 percent of residents as 65 or older and only 3.2 percent under 5. The 2020 census put the median age at 48.2.

  • A high share of older residents often means estate sales, downsizing and moves to be near family.
  • With 88.9 percent of homes owner-occupied, most sales here are owner-to-owner rather than investor deals.
  • Sun City, the age-restricted community reached by Del Webb Boulevard, is its own submarket and has its own garbage arrangement according to the village.

What drives the local economy and the roads around Huntley?

Growth in new businesses and distribution warehouses, especially along Illinois Route 47, has shaped the last decade. A small downtown keeps restaurants and shops. Route 47 is the main north-south road and runs nearly seven miles through the village. It was widened from two to five lanes in 2011, carries over 20,000 vehicles a day, and meets I-90 at a full interchange that was finished in November 2013.

Algonquin Road, a four-lane divided highway, runs east toward Algonquin and Lake in the Hills, and Main Street connects west toward Marengo and Harmony Road. Huntley-Dundee Road leads east to the Carpentersville and Dundee area. The Union Pacific Belvidere Subdivision passes through, and many local industries sit near the tracks.

Huntley once planned a stop on a proposed Metra intercity line from Rockford to Chicago, but it withdrew over concerns about its downtown. A listing can point to the I-90 and Route 47 access as a practical selling point.

Which schools and services come with a Huntley address?

Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village. Huntley High School is on Harmony Road, and the middle schools are Marlowe in Lake in the Hills and Heineman in Algonquin. Elementary schools include Leggee in Huntley, Martin and Chesak in Lake in the Hills, and Conley and Mackeben in Algonquin.

  • The Huntley Fire Protection District covers about 55 square miles and serves all village residents.
  • The Huntley Area Public Library is on Ruth Road. The Hampshire Township part of the village is served by the Ella Johnson Memorial Public Library.
  • The Huntley Park District runs the recreation center on Mill Street.
  • Residential garbage goes through a single village-wide hauler with Monday pickup, except apartments and Sun City.
  • Overnight parking on village streets is prohibited from 2 a.m. to 6 a.m., which matters when buyers or movers visit.

Huntley is a home rule municipality with an elected village president and a six-member board of trustees.

Does Huntley charge a transfer stamp, and what else applies at closing?

No. The village's FAQ says Huntley does not require a real estate transfer stamp, and it also says the village does not require village stickers.

State law still applies. Illinois also taxes the transfer of title itself under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be left out of the taxable value if the deed says so. Ask the title company which county charges apply to a McHenry County parcel and which to a Kane County parcel.

Most home improvements in the village need a permit, and Development Services at 847-515-5252 can confirm whether a past project was permitted. If you finished a basement, deck or similar work, find the permit paperwork before you list.

Who handles property tax questions for a Huntley house?

The village points owners to the county and township that match the parcel. The table lists each contact as the Huntley FAQ prints it.

Source: Village of Huntley FAQ page. The back of your tax bill also shows the taxing districts that levy against the house, and the closing attorney can use it to prorate the bill at closing.

What village rules does a buyer inherit with a Huntley house?

Buyers often ask about local rules before they make an offer, and the village FAQ answers several of them.

  • Watering follows a four-tier color-coded conservation program (red, yellow, orange and green), with signs posted around the village.
  • The village applies the McHenry County Open Burning Ordinance to all property inside its limits, and because lots are small, leaf burning is essentially illegal for most homeowners.
  • There is no village pet license, but McHenry and Kane counties both require rabies tags for dogs.
  • A garage sale needs no permit, though signs may go only on private property.
  • Recreational vehicle parking and storage fall under Zoning Code Section 156.106.
  • Yard waste is collected from April 1 to November 30, and the village runs a branch pick-up program twice a year.

Handing a buyer this short list in advance saves questions during negotiations, and it shows the house has been looked after.

How can you sell a Huntley house quickly?

Three routes are open, and the right one depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

  • Hire an agent and list. This tends to reach the most buyers, and Huntley's owner-heavy market suits it when the house is in good shape.
  • Sell it yourself. You keep the whole process in your hands, including the contract and the disclosures.
  • Take a cash offer. It can work for an inherited house, a rental, or a place that needs repairs you do not want to fund, and the closing date can be set around your plans.

Before choosing, confirm the county for the parcel, collect any permit records, and ask the water billing office about a final reading. With no village stamp to buy, Huntley sales can move on a short schedule once the contract is signed.

More questions about Huntley, IL

What is the population of Huntley, IL?

The Census Bureau estimated 29,132 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 27,740.

Does Huntley require a real estate transfer stamp?

No. The Village of Huntley's FAQ states that it does not require a real estate transfer stamp or village stickers. Illinois state transfer tax still applies.

Which counties is Huntley in?

McHenry County and Kane County. Land north of Kreutzer Road is in Grafton Township, and most land south of it is in Rutland Township.

Which school district serves Huntley?

Huntley Community School District 158 serves the village, with Huntley High School on Harmony Road.

Who do I call about property taxes on a Huntley house?

Call the McHenry County Assessor's Office at 815-334-4290 or Kane County at 630-232-5950, depending on where the parcel lies. The township numbers are in the table above.

How does selling a house in Lake in the Hills work?

Three paths are open to an owner: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or sign with an investor who pays cash and skips the repair list. Whichever route you pick, a sale in Lake in the Hills runs through the same local pieces: Village Hall for permits and contractor questions, the three fire protection districts and four school districts that overlap the village, and the McHenry County Recorder for the deed.

Lake in the Hills sits in McHenry County, northwest of Chicago, along the Randall Road corridor. The 2020 census counted 28,982 residents, and that number has barely moved since. A seller here is usually working with a house built after the 1990s growth wave, or with an older lakeside cottage in the east side of the village, and the two behave very differently at sale time.

How did Lake in the Hills grow into the village buyers see?

It is a former summer-cottage community that turned into a commuter suburb. A federal judge started the lakeside settlement around Woods Creek Lake in 1923, vacationers from Chicago slowly became year-round residents, and the village was formed on November 29, 1952. Growth exploded in the 1990s: roughly 17,000 people were added in that decade, and the village issued more than 1,000 residential building permits in 1995 alone.

Randall Road now splits the village into an older East Side and a newer West Side, and Algonquin Road marks the boundary with the village of Algonquin. Buyers tend to compare houses by subdivision, so it helps to know which one yours belongs to.

  • The Old Section: four older neighborhoods (Original, Indian, Tree and Presidents, named for their street themes) near the lake, with mixed architecture instead of tract styling.
  • Boulder Ridge: a gated community north of Algonquin Road with the village's only 18-hole golf course.
  • Big Sky and Harvest Gate: early subdivisions west of Randall Road, split by Woods Creek and close to the village hall and Lincoln Prairie Elementary.
  • Spring Lake Farm: an early-1990s subdivision south of Miller Road with both single-family and multifamily housing.

Which school and fire districts cover a Lake in the Hills address?

Four school districts share the village, so the district tied to your street matters to many buyers. Consolidated District 158 covers most of the dense western half, District 300 covers the older eastern sections, and Elementary District 47 and Community High School District 155 reach a small central slice.

That means a seller on the west side may market Huntley High School, while a seller on the east side points to Jacobs High School in Algonquin, and the central pocket feeds Crystal Lake South and Crystal Lake Central. Elementary names in the village include Lake in the Hills Elementary, Lincoln Prairie, Glacier Ridge, Canterbury, Woods Creek, May Chesak, Hannah Martin, Mackeben and Marion Conley, depending on the boundary.

Fire service is also split. The village says three separate districts, the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District, Crystal Lake Fire Rescue and the Huntley Fire Protection District, serve different parts of town, each with its own taxing authority. Check your tax bill or call the district before you describe the house in a listing.

What does federal data say about homes in Lake in the Hills?

Census Bureau QuickFacts describes a village of owners: more than four in five households own their home. Population was estimated at 28,590 in July 2025, a dip of 1.4 percent from the 2020 starting point.

With nearly three people per household and more than a quarter of residents under 18, three- and four-bedroom floor plans are the common fit. A commute near half an hour fits the Randall Road drive toward Interstate 90, which the village puts about seven miles south.

Do you need a permit before selling a Lake in the Hills house?

No permit is needed just to sell, but any construction, remodeling that changes structure, plumbing, electrical or heating, and many replacements need one first. Village Hall at 600 Harvest Gate reviews both zoning and building code before a permit issues, and the Village Hall number printed on its permit page is 847-960-7400.

  • Applications can be emailed as PDFs to the community development address, dropped in the box at the Village Hall parking lot entrance, or brought in person.
  • Air conditioners, furnaces, roofing, siding, water heaters and water softeners can be permitted through the online portal.
  • Contractors must be licensed by the village; call Village Hall to confirm a name before hiring.
  • Plumbing inspections are offered Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from noon to 4 p.m.
  • Village approval does not depend on your homeowner association, so check the association separately.

If a past owner finished a basement or deck and you cannot find the permit, ask Village Hall what is on file for the address before a buyer's inspector asks. A buyer paying cash for the house as-is may accept that risk, but a lender-backed buyer often will not.

Which village rules show up on a showing day?

Winter and noise rules are the ones sellers trip over. The village plows most streets, aims to clear them 6 to 10 hours after snow stops, and bans on-street parking once an inch has fallen under Municipal Code Section 41.03. County crews handle roads such as Algonquin, Lakewood, Randall and Ackman, and the state handles Routes 31 and 47.

Property owners clear their own sidewalks and driveways, and snow belongs in the yard, not the street. Garbage cans go to the curb at 6 p.m. or later the evening before pickup and should be stored out of sight otherwise. Construction, lawn work and personal snow removal are exempt from the noise limits only between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m., which matters if you are rushing repairs before listing.

What happens at recording and transfer in McHenry County?

Deeds are filed with the McHenry County Recorder, and the state transfer tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 is fifty cents per $500 increment of the value written on the declaration. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-25 the paperwork is due with the deed or inside three business days of the transfer, whichever comes first, with a seller's and a buyer's signature (or those of their agents).

The county's own checklist for good recordings is worth reading before closing:

  • The online MyDec declaration must read "Closing Completed."
  • A deed needs the grantee's address and the full McHenry County legal description.
  • A Plat Act affidavit must accompany a deed that uses a metes and bounds description.
  • A signed exemption paragraph or a PTAX-203 or MyDec declaration must come with every deed.
  • Documents need a half-inch clean margin and a clear 3 by 5 inch space in the upper right corner.

Ask the McHenry County Recorder whether a county or village transfer fee applies to your parcel, since this brief covers only the state rate.

When does a cash offer fit a Lake in the Hills sale?

A cash sale makes sense when the house needs work a lender's appraiser would flag, when you inherited a home you cannot maintain, or when the calendar matters more than squeezing out the top price. Houses with deferred maintenance, an association dispute or a pending violation notice are typical examples, since each can slow a conventional listing.

Compare any offer against a listing by asking the buyer to state the closing date, who pays recording and transfer charges, and whether repairs are priced in. Get that in writing, then confirm the title company will handle the PTAX declaration and the recorder submission.

More questions about Lake in the Hills, IL

What if my Lake in the Hills house has open permits?

Yes, but expect the buyer or title company to ask about them. Contact Village Hall at 600 Harvest Gate to see what is open for the address, then either finish the inspections or disclose the work. A cash buyer may take the house with the open item priced in.

Which office records my deed?

The McHenry County Recorder records deeds for Lake in the Hills. The county's recording checklist requires a completed transfer declaration, the grantee's address and the full legal description, and the MyDec record must show that closing was completed.

Do homeowner associations affect permits here?

Village approval is based on codes and zoning, not on your association. Many Lake in the Hills subdivisions still have their own rules, so get any needed association sign-off in addition to the village permit.

Who handles snow removal on my street?

It depends on the road. The village clears most local streets, county crews handle Algonquin, Lakewood, Randall and Ackman Roads, the state handles Routes 31 and 47, and some roads belong to property owner associations. Call 847-960-7500 for a specific street.

How is the state transfer tax stated?

The state sets the tax in 35 ILCS 200/31-10 and applies it to the value shown on the declaration. A deed that says it conveys the property subject to a mortgage lets the unpaid mortgage balance be left out of the base.

Lansing at a glance

Selling in Lansing?
We buy Lansing houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What are your options for selling a house in Lansing?

A Lansing owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer for the house as-is. Lansing is a Cook County village on the Indiana line, so a sale involves three layers of paperwork: the village for its seller certificate, the Cook County Clerk for recording and county transfer tax, and the State of Illinois for the transfer declaration.

Lansing is a home rule community, which gives the village more room than most to write its own local rules. That is why this page spends time on the village's own requirements instead of repeating generic Illinois advice.

Where is Lansing and what is the housing stock like?

Lansing sits 6.9 miles south of the Chicago city limits at 138th Street and about 25.6 miles from the Loop, on an ancient Lake Michigan shoreline known as the Calumet Shoreline. Its neighbors are South Holland and Calumet City to the north, Thornton and Glenwood to the west, Lynwood to the south, and Munster and Hammond in Indiana to the east. The land area is just over 7.4 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 29,076 residents.

The first settler family arrived in 1843, the Lansing brothers followed in 1846, and the village incorporated in 1893. Dutch and German farmers came first, and the industrial growth of the Calumet region later brought Irish and Eastern European families. A seller can mention that long local history, since many buyers like an established village.

Transportation options include Pace bus service, the Grand Trunk Western Main Line between Chicago and Port Huron, and the South Shore Line station at Munster Ridge in Indiana, which opened to riders on March 31, 2026. There is no published Pace connection to that station yet, so most commuters still drive.

What do Census numbers say about Lansing homes?

Lansing's QuickFacts profile shows the most affordable housing of the four Illinois villages in this group, with a median owner-occupied value well under the others. The estimated population was 28,068 in July 2025, which is 3.5 percent below the 2020 estimates base.

The median monthly cost for owners without a mortgage is $825, so households that have paid off the house carry modest bills. Those owners sometimes consider a quick as-is sale after an inheritance or a move, and the cost figures help a buyer judge what the house is worth to keep.

Which schools serve Lansing homes?

Two elementary districts and one high school district serve the village. District 158 runs Coolidge, Lester Crawl, Oak Glen and Reavis schools plus Memorial Junior High for grades 6 to 8. Sunnybrook District 171 runs Nathan Hale for PreK through grade 4 and Heritage Middle School for grades 5 to 8. Thornton Fractional South High School in District 215 takes students for grades 9 to 12.

Private and parochial options listed by the village include St. Ann, Lansing Christian, Trinity Lutheran, Saint John Lutheran and Eagle Christian Academy. Buyers with children usually start by asking which of the two elementary districts covers a given address, so have the answer ready.

What does Lansing require when a house changes hands?

The village, not the county, attaches its own condition to the sale. Cook County Clerk's list of municipal transfer taxes shows Lansing's rule, enacted May 21, 2013: the seller is liable, and a certificate of payment from the village must be attached to the recording. The list says there is no fee exemption.

  • Ask the Lansing Municipal Center at 3141 Ridge Road (the village's number on the Clerk's list is 708-895-7200) how to obtain the certificate before the closing date.
  • The Clerk's page says stamp purchasers should confirm the final amount with the municipality, since the published list carries no legal weight.
  • The state tax is 50 cents per $500 and the county tax is 25 cents per $500 on that list, with the seller named as the liable party for both.

Build the certificate into your closing timeline. The Clerk's list requires the certificate to be attached to the recording, so a missing one can hold up the buyer's possession.

What should a buyer and seller know about water, vacancies and permits?

Lansing's new-resident page sets a few rules that catch buyers off guard. Residential water service needs a deposit of $100, paid at the Municipal Center after possession, with a driver's license and the closing documents. If a property has sat vacant four months or longer, the Building Commissioner must inspect it before that deposit is taken.

That last rule matters if you are selling a vacant or inherited house. Expect the buyer to need an inspection before water can be turned on, and consider scheduling it yourself so the sale is not held up.

  • Permits: the Building Department handles permits, contractor licenses and property maintenance, and its office number is (708) 895-7193. Four property maintenance inspectors investigate complaints and issue violation notices.
  • Vehicle stickers: new residents have 30 days to buy village stickers, and you must bring a closing document or lease.
  • Trash: each single-family home gets three toters, and yard waste collection runs April 1 through November 30.

What move-out details does the village list for Lansing households?

The village's new-resident page also covers the small items a seller can hand over in a folder. Vehicle stickers go on sale May 1 each year and expire June 30, and a buyer who moves in mid-year has 30 days to buy one. Dog and cat tags are required annually and go on sale in mid-May at the Municipal Center.

Garbage and recycling use village-issued toters that stay with the house, and leaves go in the green-lidded toter or brown paper bags from April 1 through November 30. Tree trimming is the property owner's job. For utilities, the page points buyers to ComEd for electricity and Nicor Gas for gas. Leaving the toters, the service numbers and any pet or sticker records for the buyer shortens the first week after closing.

Does flooding affect selling a house in Lansing?

It can. The village keeps a flood information section covering the Little Calumet River, flood hazard, flood proofing and protection regulations, and it links to resources for Cook County residents affected by the storms and flooding of August 16 to 19, 2025. If your lot is near the river or has a history of basement water, gather any repair receipts and elevation or insurance paperwork before you list.

FEMA publishes the official flood maps at its Map Service Center, and the village can point you to its own guidance. A buyer's insurance quote often decides whether a deal closes, so being open about past water problems protects the sale.

When is a cash offer a reasonable choice in Lansing?

With a median owner-occupied value of $177,000, a large repair bill takes a bigger share of the price in Lansing than it would at a higher value. If the roof, sewer line or basement needs work and you would rather not manage contractors, a cash buyer who takes the house as-is removes that step. Ask for a closing date in writing, ask who pays for the seller certificate, and confirm the buyer's title company will submit the transfer declaration.

More questions about Lansing, IL

Who pays transfer tax when selling in Lansing?

The seller. The Cook County Clerk's municipal list names the seller as the liable party for the state tax, the Cook County tax and Lansing's own certificate of payment. Confirm final amounts with the village before closing.

Do I need an inspection before the buyer gets water?

Only if the property has been vacant four months or more. In that case the Building Commissioner must inspect before the $100 water deposit is accepted. An occupied house goes straight to deposit and application at the Municipal Center.

Which office handles permits in Lansing?

The Building Department at the Lansing Municipal Center handles permits and contractor licenses. Call (708) 895-7193 before starting any home improvement. Most improvements need a permit.

Which high school serves Lansing?

Thornton Fractional South High School, part of District 215, serves the village. Elementary students attend either District 158 or Sunnybrook District 171 depending on the address.

Is Lansing in a flood-prone area?

Parts of the area sit near the Little Calumet River, and the village publishes flood hazard and protection information. Check the FEMA flood map for your parcel and ask your insurer before listing.

What are the main ways to sell a house in Lockport?

Lockport owners can list through an agent, sell by owner, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house in its current condition. One local detail simplifies the money side: the city's own FAQ says Lockport does not impose a transfer tax, so the taxes at closing come from the state and the county, not the city.

Lockport is in Will County, so the deed goes to the Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet, and property tax questions go to the Will County Treasurer and Supervisor of Assessments.

What kind of city is Lockport?

Lockport sits on the east bank of the Des Plaines River just north of Joliet, with the village of Lemont about two miles north. The 2020 census counted 26,094 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 27,822 is 6.6 percent above the 2020 estimates base, the only one of the four Illinois places in this Census comparison that gained population.

The city grew around the Illinois and Michigan Canal. The original canal headquarters building from 1837 now holds a museum, the Gaylord Building (1838, local limestone) holds a restaurant and galleries, and the Norton Building (1850, built as a grain processor) houses lofts, offices and a state museum gallery. The Gladys Fox Museum sits in an 1839 church, and Lincoln Landing is an open-air park beside the canal. The city also has a Historic Preservation District with its own permit rules, which affects what an owner there can change.

Which Lockport schools and districts matter to buyers?

All of Lockport falls in Lockport Township High School District 205, whose Central Campus (opened 1910) serves freshmen and whose East Campus (opened 1964) serves sophomores through seniors. The grade-school pattern is more fragmented, and the district tied to a street can change a buyer's interest.

  • Taft School District 90 covers the southwest part of the city.
  • Milne-Kelvin Grove District 91 covers the west central part, with Milne Grove for kindergarten through grade 3 and Kelvin Grove for grades 4 to 8.
  • Will County School District 92 serves the north, with Walsh, Reed, Ludwig and Oak Prairie schools.
  • Homer District 33C serves the east and Fairmont District 89 serves the south.

Catholic options include Saints Dennis and Joseph Catholic Academy in the city, plus Providence Catholic in New Lenox and Joliet Catholic Academy nearby.

What do Census figures show about Lockport homes?

QuickFacts lists Lockport as an owner-heavy city with a large share of college graduates and long commutes.

The 35.3-minute average commute is the longest of the four comparison places on the same Census table. Commuters have alternatives: Lockport has a Metra Heritage Corridor station with weekday rush-hour service to Chicago Union Station, Pace routes 832 and 834 reach Joliet, and Interstate 355 runs through the area.

Which Lockport permits and rules affect a sale?

Most of the pre-listing questions are answered by the city's Building Department FAQ. Over-the-counter permits cover HVAC, water heaters, roofs, siding and windows, and other work goes through plan review that typically takes 10 to 14 business days when the submission is complete. A remodeling permit stays valid six months, and a new building permit one year.

  • Contractors working in the city must register with the Building Department before starting, and work hours are 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Saturday and 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday.
  • Owners may do their own work on an owner-occupied single-family home, but the city does not allow house flipping unless every tradesperson registers.
  • A swimming pool 24 inches or deeper needs a permit and a four-foot barrier with a self-closing, self-locking gate.
  • Changes inside the Historic District need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Planning Department.

The FAQ also covers the plat of survey: look in your closing papers first, since the city usually holds a plat only for homes built since 2002. A new survey costs about $500 by the city's estimate.

What is the landlord program and who does it affect?

If the house has been rented, the Code Enforcement Department runs a landlord rental property registration with health and life safety inspections. Its duties also include abandoned vehicles, grass over 8 inches, exterior maintenance on dilapidated buildings, pool barrier violations and signs without permits.

An investor buying a Lockport rental should ask the department how the registration transfers, and a seller moving out of a former rental should ask whether the property is registered. Code Enforcement answers at 815-838-0549, extension 2153 for the assistant line.

How do roads, parks and flood maps shape a Lockport listing?

Buyers ask who plows and repairs the street. In Lockport the answer varies: the Illinois Department of Transportation maintains Route 7 (9th Street and 159th Street), Route 53 (Broadway), Route 171 (State Street and Archer Avenue) and New Avenue, Will County maintains roads such as 143rd Street, Briggs Street and Cedar Road, and the city maintains streets including Farrell Road and Division Street west of Briggs.

Parks add to the pitch. The Lockport Township Park District, created in 1945, manages 38 parks, and Dellwood Park hosts October haunted attractions. For flood risk, the city points owners to FEMA's Flood Map Service Center and its Engineering Department, because a floodplain location can change building requirements and insurance needs. Pull the map for your parcel before you list, and note that a private-line sewer or water repair stays with the owner while main-line problems belong to the city.

How do water, trash and snow rules work at closing?

The city lets sellers order a final water reading by calling the Water Department at 815-838-0549, option 3, with the closing date, a forwarding address for the final bill and the purchaser's name. Water and garbage bills mail around the first of the month and are due by the 15th.

Trash and recycling run through an inclusive city contract with Waste Management, with yard waste collected from April 1 through the first week of December. For winter, the city maintains 108 miles of roadway with 11 snowplow trucks and aims to clear streets within 24 hours after snow stops. Parking on city streets is banned when snowfall exceeds 2 inches, and curb parking is barred from 3 to 6 a.m. The city replaced vehicle stickers in 2015 with a municipal electric excise tax, so a buyer has no sticker to purchase.

On the private side, the homeowner owns the sewer line from the house to the main, and a home with a sprinkler system needs an annual backflow (RPZ) test report before the system is turned on each season.

What happens with recording and tax in Will County?

Recording happens at the Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet (815-740-4637 on the county directory), and the Illinois transfer declaration and 50-cent-per-$500 state tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 still apply even though Lockport adds nothing. Property tax bills come from the Will County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's page explains that delinquent taxes can be sold at the annual tax sale, with homeowners typically getting one to three years to redeem. Ask the treasurer about current balances before you set a closing date.

A cash buyer in Lockport should confirm who pays recording fees and whether any unpaid city water or code fines must be cleared first.

More questions about Lockport, IL

Does Lockport charge a city transfer tax?

No. The city's FAQ says Lockport does not impose a transfer tax. The state tax of 50 cents per $500 under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 still applies to the sale.

How do I order a final water reading?

Call the city Water Department at 815-838-0549, option 3, with the closing date, the address for the final bill and the purchaser's name. Bills mail around the first of the month and are due by the 15th.

Can I do my own repairs before selling?

Yes, if you own and live in a single-family home, though permits are still required and the city bars house flipping unless all trades register. Painting, tuckpointing and fixture swaps need no permit outside the Historic District.

Which school district covers my Lockport address?

Every address is in Lockport Township High School District 205. Grade school depends on the street: Taft 90, Milne-Kelvin Grove 91, Will County 92, Homer 33C or Fairmont 89. Confirm with the district before listing.

Is a historic district permit different?

Yes. Changes within the Historic District go through the Certificate of Appropriateness process with the Planning Department, and the list of exempt ordinary repairs does not apply there.

What kind of village is Round Lake Beach?

Round Lake Beach is a village in northern Lake County, incorporated on February 5, 1937, and covers about 5.2 square miles. The 2020 census counted 27,252 residents, down from 28,175 in 2010. It is the principal city of the Round Lake Beach, McHenry and Grayslake urban area, which had 261,835 people in 2020, and the village has the second highest Latino population in Lake County after Waukegan.

Population grew from 1,892 in 1950 to 25,859 in 2000, so the housing stock reflects building over several decades. Major streets include Monaville Road, Fairfield Road, Rollins Road, Cedar Lake Road, Hook Drive and Hainesville Road.

The village spends roughly $3 million to $4 million a year on infrastructure improvements using tax increment financing and motor fuel tax money, according to Wikipedia.

What do Census figures say about Round Lake Beach homes?

QuickFacts estimates the population at 26,902 on July 1, 2025, down 1.3% from the 2020 base. From 2020 to 2024 it counts 8,537 households averaging 3.16 people, and 79.3% of housing units are owner-occupied.

How do commuting and jobs affect demand in Round Lake Beach?

The village has a station on Metra's North Central Service, which runs between Antioch and Chicago Union Station on weekdays. Pace Route 570 connects Round Lake Beach with Fox Lake, Grayslake and other points. Census data puts the mean commute at 30.4 minutes, and 72.9% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

The train station and the road links along Rollins Road and Cedar Lake Road are the usual selling points for a commuter. Households here are large, at 3.16 people each, so family-sized houses are the norm.

Which school district serves Round Lake Beach?

Round Lake Area School District 116 serves the village and four other communities. The district reports about 6,000 students, 10 schools and roughly 1,000 staff members, with a four-year graduation rate of 88% for 2024. Round Lake High School reopened in 2016 after a renovation that added 27 learning lab classrooms, science labs and a new gymnasium.

The district opened a school-based health center in 2014 in partnership with the Lake County Health Department and runs an in-district preschool program for about 200 students. Families asking about schools usually want to know the attendance boundary for one address, which the district can confirm.

What is the occupancy permit, and when do you need it?

Round Lake Beach requires every residential property to obtain an Occupancy Permit before it is sold. The permit moves water and sewer service from the seller to the buyer and confirms the exterior is maintained and up to code. The village asks you to contact it at least two weeks before closing.

  • Fill out the online occupancy application, select the address and choose the Occupancy permit type.
  • Attach photos of the water meter.
  • After the application is accepted, pay the $60 fee by emailed link.
  • The inspection is scheduled after payment. It covers the exterior only, and no one has to be present.
  • Five days before closing, email a photo of the inside meter reading and the outside receiver reading, if there is one, so the final water bill can be calculated.

The village's FAQs add that the final water bill must be paid before the buyers can pick up the occupancy certificate. Call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 as soon as the closing date is set.

How do water bills and deposits work during a sale?

Water and sewer bills go out every two months, in January, March, May, July, September and November, and a bill unpaid after its due date can carry a 10% late fee under the village FAQ. New owners pay a $100 deposit billed on the first bill, refundable only after ownership or tenancy changes and the final bill is paid in full.

The village's billing page lists its water and sewer charges per 1,000 gallons plus per-bill customer and sewer fees, and it adds a phosphorus surcharge for regional treatment at the Fox Lake facility. Rates have been adjusted in 2026, so ask Village Hall for the schedule that applies to your final bill.

What if the house is a rental?

Rental owners follow a separate annual certification program. Landlords receive a notice in early to mid October with their inspection times, deadlines and fees. Requirements include a submitted application, the certification fee, a passed inspection with deficiencies resolved, current Crime Free certification, and no outstanding liens or payments owed to the village. Missing the deadline brings a $100 late fee and a two-week extension, and after that the property can go to adjudication with an additional $1,500 fine and liens.

Landlords new to the village must attend a Crime-Free Housing seminar, or show proof of certification from another Chicagoland municipality. Call 847-546-2351 for seminar information. A seller with tenants should confirm the certification is current before accepting a contract.

What transfer taxes and property tax dates apply in Round Lake Beach?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division collects the state and county transfer taxes at recording: 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county, issued as a single stamp. The county's pamphlet says the tax may be paid by buyer or seller, so check your contract. A state transfer declaration (PTAX-203) accompanies the deed unless an exemption statement is signed. The Recording Division is at 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575.

The county's list of communities that require their own transfer stamp names Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Round Lake Beach is not on it, though you should confirm with Village Hall.

Lake County's 2025 tax calendar, payable in 2026, mailed bills May 1 and set the first installment due June 4 and the second due September 4. Those dates have passed, and the county posts each year's calendar on its Treasurer pages.

More questions about Round Lake Beach, IL

Do I need an occupancy permit to sell in Round Lake Beach?

Yes. Residential properties must obtain an Occupancy Permit before sale. The fee is $60 and the inspection covers the exterior only.

How early should I start the permit?

At least two weeks before closing. The village also schedules the final water reading about 3 to 5 days before closing, so call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 once the date is set.

Does anyone need to be home for the inspection?

No. The occupancy inspection is exterior only, and the village says no one is required to be present.

What is the water deposit for new owners?

A $100 deposit billed on the buyer's first water and sewer bill. It is not refundable until the property changes ownership or tenancy and the final bill is paid in full.

Which office records a Round Lake Beach deed?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. It collects the state and county stamps and records the stamped deed.

How does selling a house in Oak Forest, Illinois work?

Oak Forest sellers deal with Cook County recording and a handful of city programs for rentals, vacant buildings and code upkeep. The city's own rules are light for an owner-occupied house, but a former rental or empty property brings extra registration questions.

Oak Forest sits about 24 miles south-southwest of downtown Chicago in Bremen Township, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 26,792 residents. The 2020 census count was 27,478. The city covers about six square miles and is largely ringed by Cook County Forest Preserves, which is where its name comes from.

Start with three questions: who holds title, whether anyone has rented the house, and whether any code notice is open. Those answers decide how long the sale takes.

What is the history and layout of Oak Forest?

The name goes back to the 1880s, when the oak stand around Cooper's Grove along the Rock Island railroad was called the Oak Forest. In 1907 Cook County approved a second poor farm and infirmary near 159th Street and Cicero Avenue, and workers and relatives settled around the railroad stop. Residents voted to incorporate as a village in 1947, and it became a city in 1971.

  • US Route 6 (159th Street) and Illinois Route 50 (Cicero Avenue) are the main crossing roads, and Central Avenue works as the main street.
  • Interstate 57 clips the southeast corner, with the 167th Street exit nearest.
  • The Oak Forest Metra station at 159th and Cicero is on the Rock Island District line to LaSalle Street, and Pace routes 354, 364 and 383 serve the city.
  • Public elementary districts include Forest Ridge District 142, Arbor Park District 145 and Tinley Park District 146. Oak Forest High School is part of Bremen District 228, and some areas feed other high schools.
  • The city has seven wards, each with an alderman, and South Suburban College is the community college district.

Oak Forest Hospital of Cook County, a long-term care facility, remains a landmark at the Cicero Avenue site.

What do Census figures say about Oak Forest homes?

More than eight in ten Oak Forest households own their home. The table gathers the figures a seller can use to frame expectations.

With a mean commute of almost 32 minutes, train access at the Cicero Avenue station and quick reach to I-57 are worth stating in a listing.

Does Oak Forest charge a city transfer tax?

The Cook County Clerk's municipal transfer tax list, updated October 2025, has no line for Oak Forest. It does list Oak Lawn, Worth, Midlothian and Country Club Hills nearby, which shows the list covers neighboring suburbs. The Clerk adds that stamp buyers should confirm with the municipality, so call City Hall at 708-687-4050 before closing.

The state and county taxes apply to every Cook County sale. The Clerk shows the State of Illinois at 50 cents per $500 and Cook County at 25 cents per $500, with the seller liable. The state rate is set by 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and the PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

What rental and vacancy rules could affect an Oak Forest sale?

Oak Forest regulates rentals more closely than many suburbs, so a house that was ever leased may carry a registration trail.

  • All rental properties must be registered under the Crime Free Multi-Housing ordinance, with a license for each calendar year. As printed, the fee is $100 for one to five units, $150 for six to ten, and rises to $500 for 41 or more.
  • Landlords complete a seminar, a physical security inspection, background checks for new tenants age 18 and over, and a city lease addendum. Missing records can bring a fine of up to $750.
  • Apartment and condominium buildings are registered and inspected every year, with inspections from May 1 through September 30.
  • Vacant buildings must be registered, with a $700 fee and required inspections.
  • A short-term vacation rental license costs $50 a year, requires the owner to live in the home as a primary residence for nine of twelve months, and requires $1,000,000 per occurrence in liability insurance.

Foreclosure notices and confirmation orders go to the city's Property Maintenance Coordinator at 15440 S. Central Avenue, and code questions go to Property Maintenance at 708-444-4846.

How does the property maintenance code touch a sale?

The city enforces the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local amendments. Violation notices cite the problem, set a correction date and schedule a re-inspection, and unresolved items can bring fines.

  • Typical violations include rubbish, tall grass, inoperable or unlicensed vehicles, roof and fence repair, and grading and drainage.
  • House numbers must be at least four inches high and plainly visible from the street.
  • Recreational vehicles of 26 feet or less may be stored anywhere on a lot, those between 26 and 40 feet only in a side or rear yard, and vehicles of 40 feet or more are not permitted.

Clear any open notice before listing. An open notice has to be dealt with by someone, and it is easier to settle before a buyer's inspector sees it.

What happens at recording and closing in Cook County?

An Oak Forest deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The Clerk's fee page lists the state and county rates and the proof of payment, a rubber stamp, and the Clerk reminds filers that municipal amounts vary by location.

  • Bring a signed deed and the PTAX-203 declaration, or an exemption statement if the transfer is not a sale.
  • Pay or settle any final water bill with the city before the closing date.
  • If the house is in a trust or an estate, give the title company the trust certificate or letters of office early.
  • Ask whether the property is a single-family house, condominium or multi-unit building, since the city registers each type differently.

Who buys houses in Oak Forest, and which route fits?

With a median value of $255,100 and an owner rate above 80%, the city is mostly owner-occupied houses. Retail and health care are the largest business categories by receipts in the Census Bureau's 2022 figures, at about $196.6 million and $77.8 million.

A traditional listing suits an updated house with no open notices. A direct sale to a cash buyer suits a house that needs work, a rental with a messy license history, or an inherited home where relatives live out of state. Both routes use the same Cook County recording steps.

How is Oak Forest assessed for property tax?

Oak Forest sits in Bremen Township, one of the south and west suburb townships on the Cook County Assessor's triennial cycle of 2023 and 2026. The Bremen township assessor takes inquiries by appointment at 708-333-1591. The city's own site points owners to the Assessor's PIN search, which is needed for a building permit or an appeal.

Ask the Cook County Treasurer for the balance and installment status on the parcel, and ask the title company how the closing statement will prorate that year's bill.

More questions about Oak Forest, IL

Does Oak Forest have a municipal transfer tax?

The Cook County Clerk's October 2025 list shows no Oak Forest tax, but the Clerk tells buyers to confirm with the municipality. Call City Hall at 708-687-4050 to be sure. State and county transfer taxes still apply.

Do I need to register a rental before selling it?

Oak Forest requires every rental property to be registered each calendar year, with fees by unit count. Ask the Crime Free Housing office at 708-687-4050 extension 1295 whether your license is current.

What is the fee for vacant property registration?

The city charges a $700 registration fee for a vacant building and requires inspections. The owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest must register it.

Which township handles my assessment?

Oak Forest is in Bremen Township, on the south and west suburban reassessment cycle of 2023 and 2026. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm.

Which schools serve Oak Forest?

Elementary districts include 142, 145 and 146, and Oak Forest High School is part of Bremen District 228. Parts of the city feed Tinley Park, Victor J. Andrew or Carl Sandburg high schools, so confirm by address.

Where is Chicago Heights and how is it laid out?

Chicago Heights is a city in Cook County, Illinois, about 30 miles south of the Chicago Loop. It sits on the high ground of the Tinley Moraine, with the older Valparaiso Moraine just to the south, and covers 10.38 square miles.

The main crossroads is where Dixie Highway (Illinois Route 1) meets Lincoln Highway (U.S. Route 30). Neighbors include Homewood, Flossmoor, Park Forest, Glenwood, Sauk Village, Olympia Fields, Ford Heights and South Chicago Heights, so a seller's comparable sales often cross village lines.

  • County: Cook, with deeds recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recordings office
  • 2020 census population: 27,480, with an estimate of 26,533 for 2024
  • Nicknames: The Crossroads of the Nation and Da Heights

How did Chicago Heights become an industrial suburb?

The first recorded settlement came in 1833, when Absalom Wells built a cabin on the ridge above Thorn Creek. By the 1840s a rural community called Thorn Grove had formed around a Presbyterian church.

In the 1890s a group of Chicago developers led by Charles Wacker formed the Chicago Heights Land Association to build an outer-ring industrial suburb. Inland Steel, the Owens-Illinois Glass Company and the Ludowici Roofing Tile Company all built factories. Workers from Italian, Polish, Slovak, Lithuanian, Irish and Black families settled the East Side and Hill neighborhoods, and a downtown formed to serve the region.

In 1916 the Lincoln Highway Association agreed to route the first transcontinental highway through the city, which is where the Crossroads nickname comes from. The Great Depression hit hard because the city was so industrial, wartime orders and a Ford stamping plant brought a revival in the 1950s, and the 1970s brought decline as heavy manufacturing scaled back or left.

How has the population of Chicago Heights changed?

The city peaked at 40,900 residents in 1970 and has lost people in every census since: 37,026 in 1980, 33,072 in 1990, 32,776 in 2000, 30,276 in 2010 and 27,480 in 2020. That is a drop of about a third from the peak.

The 2020 count lists 9,261 households and a median age of 35.5. There were 10,663 housing units, 13.1 percent of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 4.0 percent and the rental vacancy rate 13.3 percent. Those figures describe a market with more supply than a growing suburb, which can make price and condition matter more to buyers.

What does a sale in Chicago Heights have to clear first?

The city charges a real estate transfer tax of $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and the seller is responsible for paying it. Three city offices must be cleared before the stamp is issued, and the city's own instructions list the order in which to visit them.

Chicago Heights transfer stamp steps, from the city's transfer stamp page and its instruction sheet
StepOffice and phoneWhat happens
1Code Enforcement, 708-756-5328For-sale inspection; unpaid liens and building violations resolved
2Water Billing, 708-756-5344Final meter reading, booked at least 3 days before the loan closing; final bill
3City Clerk, 708-756-5304Other unpaid fees or citations; transfer tax payment
4Code EnforcementCertificate of Occupancy after the final inspection passes and any escrow is posted

The clerk's office needs the completed application signed by seller and buyer, a photocopy of the new deed, the Certificate of Occupancy and the state PTAX-203 declaration. Payment must be cash, money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. Credit cards, debit cards and personal checks are not accepted, and each payment (transfer tax, exemption fee, water, escrow) is separate.

What happens at the for-sale inspection?

Code Enforcement oversees property maintenance, building safety and regulatory compliance, and its page states that it conducts residential and commercial sale and rental inspections for life-safety standards. The city's codes include the 2018 International Residential Code, the 2012 Property Maintenance Code, the 2014 Illinois Plumbing Code and the 2017 National Electrical Code.

  • Call 708-756-5328 early, because the Certificate of Occupancy depends on a passed final inspection
  • Resolve open violations or liens, or post an escrow where the city allows it
  • Ask whether the inspection date and result affect your closing schedule

Repairs that a for-sale inspection finds do not disappear in a cash sale. A buyer who takes the house as-is still has to satisfy the city's requirements, so ask Code Enforcement how an as-is transfer is handled before you accept an offer.

What if the property is vacant or in foreclosure?

Chicago Heights runs a defaulted mortgage and foreclosure property registration program, administered by Hera Property Registry. Owners, mortgagees and trustees must register online and pay a fee.

If the house has sat empty, register it, resolve the violations and gather the permit history before listing.

Which schools and colleges serve Chicago Heights?

Chicago Heights School District 170 runs twelve schools for about 3,600 students. Highland is the preschool, nine neighborhood schools serve kindergarten through fifth grade, and Chicago Heights Middle School covers grades six to eight. District 170 students then attend Bloom High School.

Parts of the city are in Flossmoor School District 161 (Serena Hills Elementary, then Parker Junior High) and in Park Forest-Chicago Heights School District 163 (Beacon Hill Primary Center, then the Michelle Obama School of Arts and Technology). Marian Catholic High School and St. Agnes School are private, and Prairie State College is the community college in the city.

What jobs and transit are in Chicago Heights?

Ford operates a metal stamping plant on Lincoln Highway that makes body panels shipped to its Chicago Assembly plant about 15 miles north. Thrall Car Manufacturing, a freight car maker, and Inland Steel were once based here. St. James Hospital closed in September 2018 after more than 100 years.

Six Pace bus routes and the Pace Chicago Heights Terminal serve the city. Metra's SouthEast Service is planned to bring commuter rail to a corridor that has had none since 1935. A buyer who values transit will ask about that line, so the seller should say only what the city has published.

How are the state and Cook County steps handled?

The state taxes the transfer of real estate at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, using the declaration filed in MyDec. When the deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk, staff check for the state stamp and for any local stamp the municipality requires.

The clerk's guidance notes that even a quitclaim deed with no money changing hands needs stamps and an exempt-transfer notation. Chicago Heights separately charges a $100 processing fee for exempt transfers and requires an original signed, notarized deed.

Should I list, sell privately or take a cash offer in Chicago Heights?

A listing reaches the most buyers, but the city's inspection and stamp process falls on the seller either way. Selling privately saves a commission and puts the paperwork on you. A cash offer on an as-is house can shorten the timeline, particularly when the house has open violations, a vacancy problem or an estate behind it.

Compare the net from each route after repairs, carrying costs and the city's fees, and ask each buyer how they will handle the for-sale inspection.

More questions about Chicago Heights, IL

Who pays the Chicago Heights transfer tax?

The seller. The city's rate is $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and it is paid at the City Clerk's office.

How do I pay the Chicago Heights transfer tax?

With cash, a money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. The city does not accept credit or debit cards or personal checks.

When should I schedule the final water reading?

At least three days before the loan closing. Call Water Billing at 708-756-5344.

Do I need an inspection to sell in Chicago Heights?

Yes for a standard sale. Call Code Enforcement at 708-756-5328 to schedule a for-sale inspection and to clear unpaid violations or liens. Exempt transfers may need a check on whether an inspection applies.

What does an exempt transfer cost?

The city charges a $100 processing fee for an exempt stamp. The original notarized deed is required and no photocopy is accepted.

Where does Belvidere sit, and what is its housing history?

Belvidere is the Boone County seat in far northern Illinois, about 12 miles east of Rockford and roughly 75 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. The Kishwaukee River runs through it, and the city is known as the City of Murals for the public art in its North State Street and South State Street historic districts, both federally listed historic districts. Wikipedia describes it as an industrial community surrounded by farms.

The first European American settlers came in 1835 and named the spot Elysian Fields; the city later took the name of Belvidere, Virginia. A railroad built south of the river in 1851 pulled the business district across the water, which is why downtown sits on the south side today. Downtown grew up along that rail line, so a house near State Street may be well over a century old, and buyers of older homes tend to ask about electrical service, roofs and basements.

Severe weather is part of local history. A tornado on April 21, 1967 killed 24 people and demolished over 100 homes, and an EF1 tornado hit the city on March 31, 2023. Keep roof invoices, storm-damage repair records and any insurance claim paperwork, since buyers and insurers ask for them.

How large is Belvidere's owner market?

The Census Bureau counted 25,339 residents in April 2020 and estimates 25,462 for July 1, 2025, a 0.5 percent gain. That steady count, rather than a boom or a slump, means prices follow condition and interest rates more than population swings.

With owners holding 70.9 percent of housing, most Belvidere sales are family homes rather than investor stock.

How do jobs and the Stellantis plant affect Belvidere home sales?

The Belvidere Assembly Plant, built in the mid-1960s, has long been the city's best-known employer. It built the Dodge Neon until 2005 and later the Jeep Cherokee, and Stellantis idled it in February 2023. Under the 2023 UAW settlement the company agreed to reopen it, so plant news moves buyer confidence in a way few other single sites do. A local agent can tell you how the latest announcements are affecting showings on your street.

  • Other manufacturers: Dean Foods and General Mills operate plants along the Kishwaukee River, and General Mills has announced a large distribution center in a newly annexed southwest area.
  • Education and training: Rock Valley College opened an Advanced Technology Center in northwest Belvidere on March 30, 2022.
  • Logistics: Walmart announced a cold storage facility project in June 2023.
  • Commute: Rockford's RMTD runs Route 24 bus service linking Belvidere and Rockford.

Sellers who need to move quickly often compare a listing timeline with a direct cash purchase, where there is no mortgage approval to wait on.

Which Belvidere school districts and amenities will buyers ask about?

Belvidere Community Unit School District 100 serves the city. Its two high schools are Belvidere High School and Belvidere North High School, its middle schools are South and Central, and its elementary schools include Lincoln, Perry, Meehan, Caledonia and Seth Whitman. Washington Academy is the district's STEM school, and the Everest Alternative Program is also listed. Buyers with children will want to confirm which attendance zone the street falls in.

Downtown draws buyers with the Boone County Museum of History, the Carnegie-built Ida Public Library (opened in 1913) and festivals such as Heritage Days. If your house is walkable to State Street, say so in the listing or offer conversation.

What does Belvidere's Building Department require for permits and repairs?

The City of Belvidere Building Department permits and inspects construction and enforces the zoning and property maintenance codes. It sits at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 300, takes calls at 815-547-7177 and keeps counter hours of 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. on weekdays. Call before starting a pre-sale project, because the city says some work needs a permit and online applications cover many permit types.

  • The city adopted the 2021 International codes (building, residential, fire, mechanical, fuel gas, existing building and energy) by Ordinance 703H on November 19, 2024, effective for permit applications after January 1, 2025.
  • State law has required carbon monoxide alarms in existing and new residences since January 1, 2007, installed within 15 feet of each bedroom.
  • Projects the city lists as commonly needing permits include siding, windows and doors, remodeling, additions, central air, plumbing, finished basements, and driveways, approaches, sidewalks and patios.
  • Landmarked buildings face added construction rules through the Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Work in the public right-of-way, such as curb cuts, sidewalks, or water and sewer line repairs, needs a Public Works permit at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 200.

Ask the Building Department for the permit history on your address before you list. An unfinished permit can surprise a buyer's inspector, while a cash buyer will usually take the house as-is and handle it afterward.

How are deeds recorded in Boone County after a Belvidere sale?

Boone County's recording page lists a standard document at $65.00, a non-standard document at $67.00 and an exempt standard document at $47.00 in a schedule effective August 1, 2018. The same page notes the statewide Rental Housing Support Fee increase that took effect July 1, 2023, so ask the office for the total before you send a check. The office takes cash and checks, wants a return envelope with postage, and does not give legal advice.

Since September 11, 2023, the county accepts transfer declarations only through the state's MyDec service, with the status set to closing completed before documents are submitted. A deed also needs a Plat Act Affidavit when it uses a metes and bounds description, designates roadway easements, or divides about five acres or less. The page lists Simplifile, CSC and EPN as e-recording providers, and a title company usually files for you.

How does Boone County assess, appeal and bill property tax?

Township assessors value every parcel as it stood on January 1, aiming for one-third of market value, and the Supervisor of Assessments equalizes townships to 33.33 percent. Taxpayers can file a complaint with the Board of Review within 30 days after publication of assessment changes or by September 10, whichever is later, on the county's forms with a market-value opinion and evidence. Acceptable evidence includes a closing statement from a recent purchase, at least three comparable sales within a year of the assessment date, a recent appraisal, or income and expense statements for investment property. A decision can be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board in Springfield within 30 days.

Bills come from the Boone County Treasurer the year after the assessment year, in two equal installments that the county describes as targeted for June and September. Treasurer contact: 1212 Logan Avenue, Suite 104, 815-544-2666. Boone County's exemptions page lists the general homestead exemption (an increase over 1977 value up to $6,000 of equalized value), a $5,000 senior exemption, a $2,000 disabled persons reduction, the senior freeze, and veterans' exemptions. If you are selling, confirm with the Treasurer which installment is paid and how the closing agent will prorate the rest.

More questions about Belvidere, IL

Is a tornado damage history a problem when selling in Belvidere?

It can be, mainly if repairs were incomplete or undocumented. The city was hit by an F4 tornado on April 21, 1967 and an EF1 on March 31, 2023, so buyers and inspectors often ask for roof and structural repair records. Gather permits and invoices, or consider an as-is sale if records are thin.

Is a transfer declaration required for a Boone County sale?

Yes. Boone County has accepted declarations only through the Illinois Department of Revenue's MyDec service since September 11, 2023, and the status must say closing completed before recording. Your title company or attorney normally completes it with you.

How much does recording a deed cost in Boone County?

The county's base schedule, effective August 1, 2018, lists $65.00 for a standard document, $67.00 for non-standard and $47.00 for government-exempt documents. The page also notes a Rental Housing Support Fee increase effective July 1, 2023, so confirm the current total with the recorder.

When can I appeal a Belvidere property assessment?

Within 30 days after assessment changes are published, or by September 10, whichever is later. File a Board of Review complaint with your estimate of January 1 market value and supporting evidence such as three comparable sales or a recent appraisal.

Does Belvidere require a city inspection before closing?

Ask the Building Department at 815-547-7177 about open permits or code violations on your address before you list. Those items can affect a buyer's lender or inspector, and the department is the city's compliance office for the property maintenance and zoning codes.
